docs.title: Nothing Held Back: Overview
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB overview Applies to: Any question about what NHB is, what it does, who it is for, what it offers, or how it works Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: What Nothing Held Back is
docs.text:
Nothing Held Back (NHB) is a transformational environment built for entrepreneurs who want to develop the thinking, skills, and standards required to build at the highest level. It is founded by Alen Sultanic.

NHB is not a content library, a networking group, or a motivational community. It is an environment designed to change how members think, how they operate, and what they build. The platform, the trainings, the coaches, the community, and the tools are the mechanism. The real product is the transformation of the entrepreneur using them.

The name reflects the operating principle. Most communities and programs hold back the strategies, frameworks, tools, and connections that matter most, keeping them gated, diluted, or behind proximity most members cannot access. NHB holds nothing back. Because when nothing is held back from a member, nothing can hold that member back.

docs.title: The core thesis
docs.text:
Most entrepreneurs are not held back by effort. They are held back by the limits of what they believe is possible and by the environments they operate in. Those limits get formed long before anyone starts a business, shaped by the people around them, the ideas they were exposed to, and the version of "successful" they inherited.

A member can work harder inside a limited frame, but they cannot build beyond it until the frame itself changes.

NHB is built around three forces that change the frame:

  1. A new way of thinking — exposure to ideas, principles, and mental models that expand what a member believes is possible and how they approach problems.
  2. A powerful environment — a space that makes a higher standard feel like the baseline, creates forward momentum, and exposes blind spots.
  3. The right people — proximity to coaches and members who operate at a higher level, whose standards raise the member's standards simply by being in the same room.

When these three forces compound, growth starts to build on itself. Results that once felt exceptional start to become the baseline.

docs.title: How NHB teaches
docs.text:
NHB's teaching approach is Socratic. Members are not handed step-by-step processes, fill-in-the-blank templates, or cookie-cutter formulas. The goal is to teach members how to think about marketing, offers, and business, so they can connect the dots and build anything.

The reasoning is simple. Systems and templates go out of date. Principles do not. A member who only knows a system becomes dependent on the next system when the first one stops working. A member who understands the principles behind every system can adapt, rebuild, and innovate in any market under any conditions.

This is why NHB teaches the why behind the how. The principles behind the tactics. The patterns behind the results. The frameworks that drive better decisions over time.

docs.title: What gets covered
docs.text:
NHB covers the full stack of modern digital marketing and business building, including:

  • Offers and offer architecture
  • Funnels and funnel economics
  • Copywriting and sales letters
  • Paid advertising across Meta, Google, YouTube, TikTok, X, and other channels
  • Conversion rate optimization and creative strategy
  • Email marketing and backend sequences
  • Webinars, challenges, live launches, and book-a-call funnels
  • Scaling and media buying
  • Positioning, pricing, and market selection
  • Brand, storytelling, and voice
  • Team building and hiring
  • The psychology of selling, buying, and influence

Each topic is taught not as a standalone tactic but as part of an integrated system. The thinking behind one discipline connects to the thinking behind the others, which is what allows a member to operate as a full-stack marketer rather than a specialist trapped in a single channel.

docs.title: What is inside the platform
docs.text: NHB is organized into four functional areas that map to how members actually work:

docs.title: Learn
docs.text:
• Live Calls — Weekly training calls with Alen and the coaching team, plus guest speakers. Live calls are where new ideas are introduced and discussed in real time.
  • Library — A searchable archive of every call, training, and insight, organized by coach, topic, and level.
  • Courses — Structured learning paths for specific skills and topics.
  • Insights — Written articles and frameworks for deeper reading.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
• Templates — Offer frameworks, funnel structures, and copy templates used by coaches and top members.
  • Swipe Files — Ad creative, landing pages, emails, and sales letters across many markets and formats.
  • Tools — Practical tools designed to shorten the execution curve.

docs.title: Get Help
docs.text:
• Fast Feedback — Members submit their work (copy, ads, offers, funnels, videos) and get direct feedback from coaches, typically delivered via Loom video.
  • Hot Seats — Live sessions where members bring a real problem to a coach and work through it in front of the community.
  • MindAI — An AI assistant trained on NHB's content, available to help members find answers, frameworks, and resources inside the platform.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
• Forum — The community's main discussion space on the NHB platform, where members post questions, share wins, and discuss what they are building.
  • Discord — A live chat layer for real-time conversation between members and coaches.
  • Meetups — In-person and virtual gatherings where members meet, build, and sharpen each other.

NHB is gradually transitioning member-to-member discussion onto the NHB platform's own forum, with Discord remaining for live chat. The Facebook group still exists but is being phased out as the platform matures.

docs.title: Who teaches
docs.text:
NHB's coaches are operators actively working on offers and businesses in real markets. They are not career educators teaching theory from the sidelines. Each coach leads a specific coaching program focused on their area of expertise, and every coach offers weekly training calls, monthly Hot Seats, and monthly Fast Feedback opportunities for members inside the NHB platform.

The coaching lineup:

  • Alen Sultanic — Fast Forward. Founder of NHB. Legendary direct response marketer with 20+ years in the game, 300+ offers built, and hundreds of top-ranked ClickBank launches. Leads Fast Forward, NHB's highest-intensity mastermind, where he works hands-on with members on offers, funnels, copywriting, ads, and scaling. Also teaches across the broader NHB membership.
  • Chris Haddad — Copywriting Mastery. One of the most respected copywriters in the direct response world. Leads the Copywriting Mastery program, teaching members the craft of persuasive writing at the mastery level.
  • Charles Kirkland — Google Ads & Scaling Lab. Known in the industry as "the Media Buyer's Media Buyer." Leads the Google Ads & Scaling Lab, teaching members Google Ads strategy and how to scale paid traffic effectively.
  • Loren Pinilis — Meta Ads & Scale Lab. Specializes in Meta (Facebook and Instagram) advertising. Leads the Meta Ads & Scale Lab program, teaching members how to build, run, and scale Meta campaigns.
  • Kevin Sheerin — Live Launch. Specializes in low-ticket offer launches and the structure required to launch them successfully. Leads the Live Launch program.
  • Brandon Vasquez — CRO Accelerator. Specializes in conversion rate optimization. Leads the CRO Accelerator program, teaching members how to systematically improve conversion on funnels, pages, and offers.
  • Isaac Lara — Email to CMO Pro. Specializes in email marketing and the broader path from copywriter or marketer into CMO-level roles. Leads the Email to CMO Pro program.
  • Robert Neckelius — AI Superpower. Specializes in AI-driven marketing, creative, and workflow. Leads the AI Superpower program, teaching members how to leverage AI tools for marketing output, research, and execution.

Each coach's individual background, program scope, and teaching specifics are covered in the dedicated coach documents inside the MindAI knowledge base. NHB also brings in guest speakers and working experts to share what they are seeing and learning in real time.

docs.title: The community
docs.text:
The NHB community spans every stage of the entrepreneurial journey. Members include new builders, copywriters, freelancers, agency owners, offer owners, and operators running businesses at every revenue level, from first six figures through nine figures. Members come from many industries, including supplements, finance, coaching, e-commerce, software, health, education, real estate, entertainment, and more.

What the community shares is not a revenue number or a business model. It is a standard for how members think, how they operate, and what they are willing to accept from themselves. That shared standard is what makes the community function as an environment rather than just a group.

Seven-, eight-, and nine-figure operators are in the community alongside new members. Experienced members share what they know, new members contribute their questions and perspectives, and everyone benefits from the proximity. The community is active every day, in every channel.

docs.title: Who NHB is for
docs.text:
NHB is built for entrepreneurs who know there is more in them than what they have currently built. It is for members who want the thinking, the skills, the environment, and the people required to move beyond where they are.

NHB is specifically built for:

  • Copywriters who want to become offer owners, CROs, or CMOs
  • Offer owners who want to scale, refine their economics, or expand into new markets
  • Agency owners who want to build better offers for their clients and grow their own businesses
  • Coaches and course creators who want to build stronger offers and scale their reach
  • Founders running e-commerce, software, or information businesses who want better marketing skills in-house
  • Freelancers who want to develop deeper skills and take on higher-value work
  • Marketers at any stage who want to understand the full stack rather than specialize narrowly
  • Entrepreneurs tired of piecing together strategy from scattered podcasts, courses, and coaches

It is for members willing to learn, willing to be challenged, willing to apply what they learn, and willing to do the work consistently over time.

docs.title: Who NHB is not for
docs.text:
NHB is not for members looking for:

  • Fill-in-the-blank templates as a complete solution
  • Guaranteed results or easy answers
  • A content library they can graze and forget
  • Hype, motivation, or inspiration without substance
  • Networking without the expectation of building

The Socratic teaching approach means members have to think, apply, and iterate. NHB does not provide step-by-step instructions that remove the thinking from the process, because that is precisely the approach that produces dependent, interchangeable marketers rather than operators who can build anything.

docs.title: How NHB is structured as a membership
docs.text:
NHB offers multiple membership levels, designed to match different stages of a member's journey and different levels of access to coaches.

  • A free tier gives new members limited access to explore the platform and see how it works.
  • A paid membership level opens full access to training, the library, the community, and monthly feedback opportunities with coaches.
  • A higher-intensity mastermind program provides direct, hands-on access to Alen and weekly deep-work sessions on member offers and businesses.

Specific pricing, features, and current plan names should always be verified against the live platform, since the membership structure evolves.

docs.title: What transformation looks like inside NHB
docs.text:
Members who engage fully with NHB tend to experience change across several dimensions over time:

  • Thinking — They see their market, their offer, and their own business more clearly. They stop guessing. They start connecting dots that were invisible before.
  • Execution — They move faster, with more intention, and waste less effort on the wrong things.
  • Offers and positioning — Their offers get sharper. Their messaging gets more specific. Their positioning attracts better customers.
  • Business outcomes — Growth compounds. New opportunities appear. Existing constraints loosen.
  • Standards — What the member is willing to accept from themselves rises. What felt like a ceiling starts to look like a floor.
  • Identity — The member becomes someone different. Not because they were told to, but because the environment made it the natural path.

NHB cannot promise any of these outcomes for any individual member, because outcomes depend entirely on what the member brings to the experience and what they do with it. What NHB can provide is the thinking, the environment, the people, the coaching, and the tools designed to make all of those outcomes possible.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Nothing Held Back is a transformational environment for entrepreneurs. It combines training, coaching, Fast Feedback, Hot Seats, community, and tools to help members develop the thinking, skills, and standards required to build at the highest level. The teaching approach is Socratic, focused on principles and mental models rather than templates and systems. The community spans every stage and many industries. The coaches are operators actively working on real businesses. The environment is designed to make a higher standard feel normal, so members rise to it naturally over time.

The name reflects the core commitment. Because when nothing is held back from a member, nothing can hold that member back.

docs.title: Account Management
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about managing an NHB account — logging in, password reset, updating payment info, changing plans, cancelling, adding team members, profile settings, billing history Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Account management covers everything a member does to administer their NHB membership outside of the actual content and community: signing in, updating payment info, changing plans, adding team members, cancelling, and managing profile settings. This doc is the quick reference for "how do I do X with my account."

docs.title: Logging in
docs.text: Members log in at app.nothingheldback.com with the email and password they set during sign-up. Sessions persist across visits. If a member is logged out, they return to the login screen.

docs.title: Password reset
docs.text:
Members who have forgotten their password can reset it at app.nothingheldback.com/auth?view=reset. They enter the email associated with their NHB account and receive a reset link. The email comes from the NHB notification system (typically support@nhbnotify.com). Members who don't receive the reset email within a few minutes should check their spam folder.

If a member is unable to reset through the standard flow, NHB support can assist directly.

docs.title: Updating payment information
docs.text:
Members can update their payment method through:

  • Their NHB account settings — typically under a Billing or Payment section
  • ThriveCart directly — at grow.thrivecart.com/updateinfo/ for members whose billing is on ThriveCart

Members should update their payment method before a failed charge to avoid interruption. If a charge fails, InfusionSoft retries up to 5 times; if all retries fail, the subscription cancels automatically and the member must re-subscribe to regain access.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
Upgrades take effect immediately. A member upgrading from Free to NHB Pro, from NHB Pro to Fast Forward, or adding a coaching program gains access to the new tier or program at the moment of checkout.

Upgrade paths inside NHB:

  • Free → NHB Pro — $500 per month or $4,500 per year
  • NHB Pro → Fast Forward — $1,000 per month with a $10,000 down payment, or $20,000 per year
  • Adding a coaching program — $1,000 per month as an add-on to an existing NHB Pro or Fast Forward membership

Members add or upgrade through the NHB platform's coaching section or through direct checkout links provided by NHB.

docs.title: Downgrading
docs.text:
Downgrades take effect at the End of Cycle. A member who requests a downgrade mid-cycle keeps their higher-tier access until the current billing period ends, at which point the downgrade processes.

When a member downgrades their base membership to Free, all coaching program add-ons automatically cancel, because coaching programs require an active NHB Pro or Fast Forward membership.

docs.title: Cancelling a membership
docs.text:
Members can cancel at any time, month-to-month. There are no long-term contracts. Cancellation takes effect at the End of Cycle, with full access retained until that point.

Cancellation paths:

  • NHB platform account settings — the primary path
  • ThriveCart — for members on ThriveCart billing
  • NHB support — for members who have difficulty cancelling through the platform

See the refund and cancellation policy document for the complete policy (no refunds, cancellation cascade for coaching programs, pause options).

docs.title: Adding team members
docs.text: NHB supports adding team members for Pro and Fast Forward accounts, and for select coaching programs.

docs.title: NHB Pro team member
docs.text:
• Cost: $250 per month per additional team member
  • Access: Team members get their own log-in under the primary member's account and full Pro-level access

docs.title: Fast Forward team member
docs.text:
• Separate "Additional FF Member" add-on available
  • Team members get their own log-in and full Fast Forward access under the primary member's account

docs.title: Coaching program team members
docs.text:
Several coaching programs have team-member add-ons available through ThriveCart:

  • Meta Ads & Scale Lab team member
  • Google Ads & Scaling Lab team member
  • Live Launch team member

Additional team members get program access under the primary member's account. Specific pricing per team member is handled at checkout.

docs.title: Profile settings
docs.text:
Members can configure their public profile through the account settings section:

  • Basic info — name, profile photo, bio, location
  • Industry and niche — market, sector, what they do
  • Work — current projects, businesses, roles
  • Links — social profiles, websites, external URLs
  • Visibility — what appears on the public profile visible to other members
  • Color mode — dark or light platform UI

See the Public Profile feature doc for full detail on what's displayed publicly.

docs.title: Notification settings
docs.text:
Members can configure which notifications they receive and through which channels (in-app, email) from the account settings. Common controls:

  • Email notifications on or off for specific event types
  • Follow/unfollow specific forum categories or members
  • Mute specific threads or categories

See the Notifications feature doc for full detail.

docs.title: Invoices and billing history
docs.text: Members can access their billing history and past invoices through their account settings. ThriveCart-billed members can also retrieve invoices directly from ThriveCart's member portal.

docs.title: Changing the email on an account
docs.text: Members who need to change their primary email (for example, switching from a personal to a work email) can do so through account settings. Note that because the email is the login identifier, changing it also changes the member's log-in credentials. NHB support can assist if a member needs to change an email and can't do it through the standard flow.

docs.title: Account restoration and returns
docs.text: A member who has cancelled and later wants to rejoin can do so by signing up again. Their previous profile and history may or may not be fully restored depending on the specific case — NHB support can help with account restoration where applicable.

docs.title: Where to find account management
docs.text:
• Main platform navigation — the account menu (typically top-right of the platform) contains settings, billing, and profile options
  • ThriveCart — for ThriveCart-specific actions like updating a card or viewing past charges

docs.title: Related documents
docs.text:
• Plans and pricing — current pricing and what each tier includes
  • Refund and cancellation policy — complete policy on cancellations, refunds, pausing
  • Public profile — what information is displayed on the member's profile
  • Notifications — managing notification preferences

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about account management, the answer should cover:

  • Logging in: app.nothingheldback.com with email and password
  • Password reset: app.nothingheldback.com/auth?view=reset
  • Updating payment: account settings or grow.thrivecart.com/updateinfo/
  • Upgrading: through the NHB platform, takes effect immediately
  • Downgrading: through the NHB platform or support, takes effect at End of Cycle
  • Cancelling: through account settings, ThriveCart, or NHB support; End of Cycle timing
  • Team members: NHB Pro $250/mo each, FF additional member available, select coaching programs support team seats
  • Profile settings: configurable through account settings
  • No refunds: all sales final, cancel before the next billing cycle

For anything account-related that the member cannot resolve through the platform, NHB support is the fallback path.

docs.title: Alen Sultanic: Founder of Nothing Held Back
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB bio document Applies to: Any question about Alen Sultanic, his background, his career, his work, his companies, his teaching, or his role inside Nothing Held Back Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Alen Sultanic is the founder of Nothing Held Back and one of the most accomplished direct response marketers of his generation. Over more than twenty years in the industry, Alen has built more than 300 offers across dozens of markets, sold over 35 product launches, and authored hundreds of number-one offers on ClickBank and other major direct response platforms.

He founded Nothing Held Back to give entrepreneurs access to the thinking, tools, coaching, and community that most communities and programs hold back behind gatekeepers, paywalls, or proximity. Inside NHB, Alen leads the Fast Forward mastermind, where he works directly with members on their offers, funnels, copywriting, ads, and scaling strategies.

docs.title: Background and early career
docs.text:
Alen's career in direct response marketing began in the mid-2000s. Between roughly 2008 and 2012, he built and launched digital products on ClickBank at a pace that was rare even in that era, producing offers across many markets and racking up a long list of top-ranked launches. That period gave him deep, hands-on experience across every part of the direct response stack: product creation, offer construction, sales copy, paid traffic, email marketing, upsells and downsells, and backend monetization.

From there, Alen expanded into a broader range of industries and roles, operating as a copywriter, offer owner, consultant, and operator across markets including supplements, finance, health, relationship advice, business opportunity, information publishing, coaching, and more. The breadth of that experience is a defining feature of how he teaches, because it gives him direct pattern recognition across markets that most marketers only ever see one or two of.

He is the founder of AlphaFour, the company behind Nothing Held Back and the infrastructure supporting the NHB community and platform.

docs.title: Consulting and advisory work
docs.text:
Alen works directly with companies, offer owners, and public figures on advertising, marketing, offer architecture, and scaling. His published consulting rates reflect the level at which he operates:

  • $5,000 per hour for consulting calls
  • $25,000 to $35,000 for a full funnel optimization review
  • $50,000 to $100,000 to build a new offer from concept to execution
  • $15,000 per month for ongoing advisory and hands-on retainer work

His consulting clients have included high-profile public figures and major brands. In Alen's own published materials, he has referenced work with Caitlin Jenner, a Mike Tyson offer, Forbes, and a range of A-list clients and large companies.

docs.title: What Alen does uniquely well
docs.text:
Alen's core talent, by his own description and by the pattern across his career, is the ability to see things other marketers cannot see. That comes from mastering both the psychology and the economics of direct response, combined with decades of pattern recognition across dozens of markets. What this translates to in practice:

  • He can enter any market and quickly identify what is working, what is missing, and where the leverage is
  • He can look at an offer, a funnel, or a sales letter and diagnose structural problems that are not obvious
  • He can connect the dots between copywriting, offer architecture, pricing, scaling, and backend economics in ways that treat them as one integrated system rather than separate disciplines
  • He can reformulate, rebuild, or redesign offers to fit changing market conditions, new platforms, or new customer segments

docs.title: Teaching philosophy
docs.text:
Alen teaches using the Socratic method. There is no step-by-step process, no cookie-cutter system, and no fill-in-the-blank template that members are handed as a complete solution. The reasoning, in Alen's own words: a cookie-cutter formula produces cookie-cutter marketers who all look the same. Great marketers have to be able to think.

What Alen teaches first is how to think. Once a member can think about marketing, offers, and business correctly, that member can connect the dots and build anything. Tactics and systems come and go. Principles do not. A member who only knows the current system becomes dependent on the next guru for the next system. A member who understands the principles behind every system can adapt and innovate in any market.

This is the source of NHB's approach and its teaching voice. Alen teaches the why behind the how — the principles behind the tactics, the patterns behind the results, and the deeper frameworks that drive better decisions over time.

docs.title: Topics Alen teaches
docs.text:
Across his trainings, hot seats, and the Fast Forward mastermind, Alen covers the full stack of direct response marketing and business building, including:

  • Offer creation, architecture, and the difference between creating, building, and running an offer
  • Funnel structures and funnel economics
  • Copywriting, sales letters, and the mechanics of persuasive writing
  • Paid advertising across Meta, Google, YouTube, and other channels
  • Email marketing and backend monetization
  • Conversion rate optimization
  • Scaling strategies, including scaling in the negative space
  • Gender-based selling and market-specific messaging
  • Push vs. pull marketing and the role of each
  • Physiological vs. psychological markets
  • Pricing strategy, including collaborative and competitive pricing models
  • Positioning, brand, and identity construction
  • Economics of competition and the three levels of economic positioning
  • Prescriptive marketing and market-specific strategic approaches
  • The 5-step sales process
  • High-performance team building and the hidden economics of scaling a team
  • Transitioning from copywriter to CRO, CMO, offer owner, or publisher
  • The psychology of selling, buying patterns, and influence
  • Isomorphic stories, narrative construction, and identity-driven messaging
  • Core beliefs and empowerment frameworks
  • First acquisition vs. second acquisition marketing

Each of these topics is taught at the principle level, not as a template, so that members come out able to apply the thinking to any market, any offer, and any product format.

docs.title: Fast Forward — program curriculum
docs.text:
Positioning: The fastest path from stuck to scaling. Twice-weekly guidance from the source.

Inside Fast Forward, members learn:

  • Everything Alen knows about building 8- and 9-figure businesses
  • Direct access to Alen twice per week through FF Theory and FF Hot Seats
  • The theory behind what actually works in marketing
  • The economic principles and psychology behind all direct response
  • Alen's complete system for scaling a business, from offer construction through backend monetization

Pricing: Fast Forward is NHB's flagship mastermind and has its own pricing structure, separate from the other coaching programs. See the plans and pricing document for current rates. Fast Forward is not an add-on; it is a membership tier that replaces NHB Pro with direct Alen access.

docs.title: Role inside Nothing Held Back
docs.text:
Alen is the founder of NHB and the leader of the Fast Forward mastermind, NHB's highest-intensity program.

Inside Fast Forward, Alen is hands-on. He reviews member offers, tweaks copy, designs hooks and angles, helps structure upsells, works through back-end call booking strategies, and gives direct feedback in the community every day. Members describe his role in Fast Forward as functioning almost like a strategic partner inside their businesses, rather than as a traditional mentor or teacher.

Inside the broader NHB membership, Alen leads weekly training calls, participates in hot seats, and contributes to the community directly. While Fast Forward members get the most direct access, all NHB members benefit from his teaching through live trainings, the library, and the overall culture of the community.

docs.title: Personal philosophy
docs.text:
A few themes run consistently through how Alen operates and teaches:

  • Skills over status. Position, fame, and titles mean nothing to him. What he values is what a person can actually do and whether they can teach others to do it too.
  • Direct response first. Even at scale, the principles of direct response remain the core. He has been vocal about the mistake marketers make when they cross seven figures and abandon direct response for "branding."
  • Nothing held back. The name of the community is not a marketing slogan. It reflects a specific commitment: give members the full picture, the real strategies, the actual tools, and the honest feedback, without gating the most important parts behind additional paywalls.
  • Ecology over exploitation. Long-term, stable businesses matter more than short-term cash grabs. The pricing, promotional, and structural decisions Alen teaches are oriented toward offers that last, not offers that peak once and die.
  • Teach thinking, not dependency. The goal is to make members capable of succeeding on their own, without needing Alen or anyone else to hand them the next answer.

docs.title: Content and public presence
docs.text: Alen is based in Charlotte, North Carolina. He publishes content and commentary across several channels, including the Nothing Held Back newsletter, social media, and as a guest on industry podcasts where he has discussed offer construction, copywriting mastery, market positioning, and the psychology behind high-converting direct response campaigns.

docs.title: Summary for answering questions about Alen
docs.text:
When a member asks about Alen, the answer should describe:

  • What he does: founded Nothing Held Back, leads Fast Forward, has 20+ years in direct response marketing
  • What he has built: more than 300 offers, over 35 product launches, hundreds of top-ranked ClickBank offers, across many markets
  • What he teaches: the full stack of modern direct response, taught at the principle level, using the Socratic method
  • How he works inside NHB: hands-on in Fast Forward, teaching across the full membership, present in the community
  • What he values: skills, thinking, direct response principles, long-term business ecology, and holding nothing back from the people he teaches

Answers should not make any specific income claims about what members will earn from learning from Alen, as covered in the NHB income and results policy. Alen's own consulting rates and the accomplishments of his career are factual and can be described directly. What any specific NHB member will earn, build, or achieve cannot be predicted or promised.

docs.title: NHB Coaching Programs

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
NHB's coaching programs are specialty-focused, add-on programs where members work directly with a specific coach every week on the area holding their business back most. Beyond NHB's content and training, coaching programs give members direct weekly access to top operators who review the member's actual campaigns, solve their specific problems, and refine their strategies in real time.

Each program is led by a coach who is actively operating in that discipline — not a career educator teaching theory from the sidelines. Every program is $1,000 per month and is an add-on to a member's existing NHB Pro or Fast Forward membership.

docs.text:

docs.title: What's included in every coaching program
docs.text:
Every coaching program gives members the same core access to their coach:

  • Weekly coaching calls. Each coach runs a weekly training call covering the core frameworks of their specialty, open to all members of their program.

This is the difference between consuming content and executing with expert oversight. The coaching programs are where content turns into action inside the member's specific business.

docs.title: How coaching programs work — the four-step process
docs.text:
Step 1 — Join a program. The member chooses their specialist based on what is holding their business back most. Pick the expert in the biggest bottleneck and get started immediately.

Step 2 — Weekly Hot Seats + Theory calls. Every week, the member brings their campaigns, funnels, copy, or problems to the coach and gets personalized guidance and solutions in real time.

Step 3 — Fast Feedback twice per week. When the member hits a roadblock between calls, they submit for Fast Feedback on designated days and get expert answers the same day.

Step 4 — Implement and grow. With weekly expert guidance, the member takes action with confidence, sees results, and continues scaling. They are not figuring it out alone anymore.

docs.title: NHB Community Guidelines
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB community guidelines document Applies to: Any question about what's allowed in the community, forum rules, reporting, content sharing, IP, community standards, member conduct Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
NHB is a community of serious operators. The community guidelines exist so the forum, Discord, Hot Seats, Fast Feedback, and every other interaction space inside NHB stay productive, respectful, and valuable for every member.

The guidelines are not complicated. Be respectful. Contribute meaningfully. Help other members grow. Don't violate NHB's policies on competitors, income claims, or content sharing. Report anything that breaks the rules.

docs.title: Core principles
docs.text:
1. Respect other members.

Every member is here to build something. That means disagreements and differing perspectives happen, which is healthy. But personal attacks, harassment, discrimination, or consistently abusive behavior toward other members is not tolerated.

2. Contribute meaningfully.

The forum, Hot Seats, Fast Feedback, and Discord are valuable because members actually engage with substance. Posts that are pure self-promotion, spam, unrelated sales pitches, or low-effort filler dilute the community and get moderated.

3. Keep it inside NHB.

Content produced inside NHB — live calls, Hot Seat recordings, coaching program materials, member-submitted work, Fast Feedback responses — is for NHB members only. Sharing it publicly, posting it on social media, or redistributing it outside the community undermines the environment and is a violation of community standards.

4. Follow NHB's specific policies.

NHB has two specific policies that intersect with community behavior:

  • Competitor policy. Do not post content that criticizes specific companies, coaches, platforms, or public figures outside NHB. This applies to forum posts, Discord messages, and Hot Seat discussions. Feedback on offers, markets, and general industry trends is fine. Public criticism of named outside parties is not.
  • Income and results policy. Do not post claims about what specific members earn, guarantees about outcomes, or predictions about results other members will achieve. Sharing your own wins is fine. Making promises about what others will earn if they follow a specific approach is not.

docs.title: What's allowed in the forum
docs.text:
Encouraged:

  • Asking substantive questions about marketing, offers, funnels, ads, copy, email, CRO, scaling, and the full range of topics NHB covers
  • Sharing wins, milestones, and progress on your own business
  • Sharing work you're getting feedback on (copy, ads, funnels, videos) and asking the community for input
  • Responding to other members with real feedback, questions, or input
  • Discussing strategy, tactics, and lessons from your own operating experience
  • Sharing resources that helped you, books, tools, or frameworks
  • Coordinating meetups, partnerships, or joint ventures

Not allowed:

  • Pure self-promotion without community value (spam posts linking only to your own offer, for example)
  • Unsolicited sales pitches to other members in DMs or threads
  • Posts designed to generate traffic to external communities, competitors, or paid services outside NHB
  • Content that violates NHB's competitor or income and results policies
  • Personal attacks on other members
  • Discrimination, harassment, or abusive behavior
  • Sharing other members' private information without consent
  • Sharing NHB content, recordings, or coach feedback publicly outside NHB
  • Illegal content, including copyrighted material shared without permission

docs.title: Content and intellectual property
docs.text:
Content you post inside NHB:

  • You retain ownership of your own work
  • You grant NHB and other members permission to view, discuss, and reference your work inside the community
  • NHB can anonymize and use aggregated patterns from community activity to improve the platform (without exposing your specific identity unless you've consented)

Content produced by NHB (calls, courses, coach materials, resources):

  • Owned by NHB
  • Licensed to members for personal use inside NHB while membership is active
  • Not licensed for public redistribution, resale, or sharing outside the community

Swipe files, templates, and resources:

  • Provided for members to use and adapt in their own businesses
  • Not for public redistribution as-is
  • Members can and should adapt them, make them their own, and apply them to their own offers

docs.title: Reporting content or behavior
docs.text:
Every post, comment, and user inside NHB can be reported through the built-in reporting system, accessed via the three-dot menu on any content. Reports go to NHB admins for review.

Reports are appropriate for:

  • Posts that violate community guidelines
  • Comments that attack or harass members
  • Users whose behavior pattern is disruptive
  • Content that violates NHB's competitor or income and results policies
  • Any content that seems designed to damage the community rather than contribute to it

Admins review reports and take action based on the specifics. Actions can include: removing the content, warning the member, suspending the member temporarily, or removing the member from the community entirely in serious cases.

docs.title: Moderation
docs.text:
NHB moderators and admins have full authority to moderate content in accordance with these guidelines. This includes:

  • Removing posts that violate guidelines
  • Closing threads that have become unproductive
  • Warning members who are repeatedly violating rules
  • Suspending or removing members whose behavior consistently undermines the community

Moderation decisions are final. Members who disagree with a moderation action can reach out to NHB support, but moderators have authority over the community spaces they oversee.

docs.title: Community standards across spaces
docs.text:
These guidelines apply uniformly across:

  • The NHB Forum (on the NHB platform)
  • The NHB Discord server
  • Hot Seat calls — live behavior on calls, including in chat
  • Fast Feedback submissions and responses
  • Meetups — in-person and virtual member gatherings
  • Any NHB-affiliated space where members interact as NHB members

Discord has its own moderation layer in addition to NHB's community guidelines; members are expected to follow both.

docs.title: What happens when guidelines are violated
docs.text:
The typical moderation progression is:

  1. First violation — content removal and a warning from a moderator
  2. Repeated violations — temporary suspension from the community
  3. Severe or consistent violations — removal from NHB without refund

The severity of any given violation is judged case-by-case. Egregious conduct (harassment, doxxing, fraudulent behavior) can result in immediate removal without warning.

Members removed from NHB for violations do not receive refunds, in line with the standard NHB refund policy.

docs.title: Questions and clarifications
docs.text: Members who are unsure whether something is appropriate to post or share should ask a moderator or NHB support before posting. When in doubt, default to not posting content that characterizes outside parties negatively, makes specific income claims about others, or shares NHB content outside the community.

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about community guidelines, the answer should cover:

  • Core principles: respect, meaningful contribution, keeping NHB content inside NHB, following NHB's policies
  • What's allowed: substantive discussion, sharing wins and work, peer feedback, meetups and partnerships
  • What's not allowed: spam, self-promotion without community value, harassment, sharing NHB content externally, criticism of named competitors, income claims about others
  • Reporting: built-in report system via the three-dot menu on any content
  • Moderation progression: content removal → warning → suspension → removal
  • No refunds: members removed for violations do not receive refunds

Any questions that push up against the boundary of the rules should be answered with the conservative interpretation. The competitor policy and income and results policy documents are the authoritative references for specific policy cases.

docs.title: NHB Frequently Asked Questions
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB FAQ document Applies to: Common member questions that cross multiple features or tiers, quick-answer reference for MindAI Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: What should a new member do first after signing up?
docs.text:
A new member's first steps inside NHB typically look like this:

  1. Complete their profile so other members can find and recognize them
  2. Join the NHB Discord for live chat
  3. Check the Live Calls page to see what's happening this week
  4. Explore the Library to browse past training on topics relevant to their business
  5. Post an introduction in the forum so the community knows who they are
  6. If they have enrolled in a coaching program, review that coach's library and attend the next available call or Hot Seat

MindAI can help a new member navigate any of these steps.

docs.title: How does a member log into NHB?
docs.text: Members log in at app.nothingheldback.com with the email and password they set during sign-up. Password reset is available at app.nothingheldback.com/auth?view=reset if a member has forgotten their password.

docs.title: Is there a mobile app?
docs.text: NHB is primarily accessed through the web platform at app.nothingheldback.com, which works on both desktop and mobile browsers. The platform is designed to be responsive on mobile. A dedicated native mobile app is not currently the primary access method, though this may evolve.

docs.title: What happens in the first week of being a member?
docs.text: The first week is typically spent orienting to the platform, attending a few live calls, exploring the Library, connecting on Discord, and if applicable starting to work with a coach. Most new members find their rhythm within two to three weeks of consistent engagement. The coaches themselves often recommend new members skip some of the exploration and just start showing up to calls and submitting work for Fast Feedback, since learning by doing inside NHB tends to work better than reading about what's available.

docs.title: What's the difference between NHB Pro and Fast Forward?
docs.text:
NHB Pro gives members full access to NHB's content, community, weekly training calls with every coach, monthly Pro Hot Seats, and monthly Fast Feedback. It is the core paid membership.

Fast Forward is NHB's flagship mastermind program where members work directly with Alen on a hands-on basis. Fast Forward members get unlimited Fast Feedback with Alen, weekly FF Theory and FF Hot Seat calls with Alen, and direct strategic work on their offers, funnels, copy, and scaling.

In short: NHB Pro is for members who want the breadth of NHB's teaching and community. Fast Forward is for members who want direct Alen time and hands-on work.

docs.title: What's the difference between NHB Pro and adding a coaching program?
docs.text:
NHB Pro teaches a member what works across all areas. A coaching program adds weekly implementation support from one specific coach on one specific discipline. The coach reviews the member's actual campaigns, solves the member's problems, and guides the member's execution in their specialty.

Pro is learning in theory. A coaching program is executing with expert oversight on real work.

docs.title: How does a member upgrade or downgrade?
docs.text:
Upgrades (Free → Pro, Pro → FF, or adding a coaching program) take effect immediately. Downgrades are processed at the End of Cycle — the member keeps their current access until the billing period ends, then the change takes effect.

When a member downgrades their base membership to Free, all coaching program add-ons automatically cancel because coaching programs require an active Pro or FF membership.

docs.title: How does a member cancel their membership?
docs.text: Members can cancel month-to-month at any time. No long-term contracts. Cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing cycle. The member retains access until that date.

docs.title: Is there a refund policy?
docs.text:
No refunds. All sales are final. Members should cancel before the next billing cycle if a plan or coaching program is not working for them.

This policy applies equally to NHB Pro, Fast Forward, and every coaching program.

docs.title: Can a member pause their membership?
docs.text: Fast Forward offers a Pause Plan for members who need to temporarily pause their Fast Forward membership. Specific terms are provided at the point of pausing. Pro and coaching programs do not currently have a formal pause option — members cancel and rejoin later when ready.

docs.title: Can a member join multiple coaching programs at the same time?
docs.text: Yes. Many members stack programs when they need deep support in multiple areas — for example, Meta Ads plus CRO, or Copywriting plus Offers. Each program adds $1,000 per month to the member's bill.

docs.title: What happens to a member's content if they cancel?
docs.text: If a member cancels their membership, they lose access to the Library, live calls, coaching programs, Fast Feedback, and other paid content. Their own submitted content (forum posts, Fast Feedback submissions) typically remains in the platform for other members but the canceled member can no longer access the platform.

docs.title: Can members add team members to their account?
docs.text: Yes. NHB Pro supports adding a team member for $250 per month per additional seat. Fast Forward supports additional FF members through a separate add-on. Select coaching programs (Meta Ads & Scale Lab, Google Ads & Scaling Lab, Live Launch) support adding team members at the program level. Each team member gets their own log-in and access under the primary member's account.

docs.title: How much does each coaching program cost?
docs.text:
Every coaching program (Meta Ads & Scale Lab, Google Ads & Scaling Lab, Live Launch, CRO Accelerator, Email to CMO Pro, Copywriting Mastery, AI Superpower) is $1,000 per month as an add-on to NHB Pro.

Fast Forward has its own pricing structure — $1,000 per month with a $10,000 down payment, or $20,000 annually if paid in full. Annual renewals for existing FF members are $12,000 per year.

docs.title: Can a member choose to just work with a coach without NHB Pro?
docs.text: No. Coaching programs are add-ons that require an active NHB Pro or Fast Forward membership. The coaching program structure depends on the member having access to the broader NHB environment, so standalone coaching without a base membership is not offered.

docs.title: Does NHB still offer the Plus plan?
docs.text: No. The Plus tier has been eliminated. The plan hierarchy is now Free (NHB) → Pro → Fast Forward. Existing content and member references to Plus are being phased out across the platform.

docs.title: Which coach should a member pick?
docs.text:
Pick based on the biggest bottleneck in the member's business right now:

  • Meta ads not scaling → Loren Pinilis (Meta Ads & Scale Lab)
  • Google Ads burning budget → Charles Kirkland (Google Ads & Scaling Lab)
  • Funnel not converting → Brandon Vasquez (CRO Accelerator)
  • Email list not producing → Isaac Lara (Email to CMO Pro)
  • Copy not selling → Chris Haddad (Copywriting Mastery)
  • Offer not dialed in → Kevin Sheerin (Live Launch)
  • Need AI systems built → Robert Neckelius (AI Superpower)
  • Want hands-on work from Alen → Fast Forward

The best rule is to choose the problem costing the member the most money right now.

docs.title: Can a member work directly with Alen one-on-one?
docs.text: Alen does not currently offer one-on-one coaching outside of Fast Forward. Fast Forward members get direct access to Alen through FF Theory calls, FF Hot Seats, and unlimited Fast Feedback. That is the path to working directly with Alen inside NHB.

docs.title: Can a member switch coaches?
docs.text: Yes, anytime. Members can cancel one coaching program and join another without penalty. Most members pick a coach based on their current bottleneck and stay because that coach gets to know their business.

docs.title: Are coaching calls recorded?
docs.text: Yes. Every live call, including Hot Seats, Coaching Theory calls, and Fast Feedback responses, is recorded and archived in the Library. Members who can't attend live can watch recordings afterward and search the full history.

docs.title: What if a member has a question about a specific topic — where do they go first?
docs.text: For quick information or to find past teaching on a topic, MindAI is usually the fastest path. For personalized feedback on the member's actual work, Fast Feedback (asynchronous) and Hot Seats (live) are the right tools. For peer input, the Forum and Discord are where the community helps each other.

docs.title: What's the difference between Fast Feedback and Hot Seats?
docs.text:
Fast Feedback is asynchronous: a member submits their work via a Google Doc, and a coach responds with a Loom video (typically) on their own schedule.

Hot Seats are live: a member submits their context ahead of time, and the coach works through it with them in real time on a live call in front of the community.

Fast Feedback is for when a member needs feedback but doesn't need to discuss it live. Hot Seats are for when live discussion and Q&A with a coach adds more value than a recorded response.

docs.title: What's the difference between the Forum and Discord?
docs.text:
The Forum (inside the NHB platform) is for long-form, searchable, durable discussion. Threads started in the forum stay findable and useful for years.

Discord is for live, real-time chat — quick questions, reactions to live calls, casual banter, and daily community presence.

Members use both, depending on whether the discussion is something they want to be findable later (Forum) or fast and conversational (Discord).

docs.title: Can a member post anything in the forum?
docs.text: The Forum is moderated, and members are expected to follow NHB's community standards. Content that targets or criticizes outside companies or public figures, makes income claims, or violates community standards may be moderated or removed. Members can report content to admins via the built-in reporting system.

docs.title: How does a member find other NHB members?
docs.text: The Rolodex, inside the Connect section of the NHB platform, is a searchable member directory. Members can also find other members through forum activity, Hot Seat attendance, coaching program communities, Meetups, and Discord.

docs.title: Does NHB have in-person events?
docs.text: Yes. NHB members organize regional meetups, NHB hosts coach-led events, and there is a separate NHB Retreat flagship event that operates as its own offering. The Meetups section on the platform shows upcoming member-organized gatherings.

docs.title: A member can't see a specific call, feature, or piece of content — why?
docs.text:
The most common reason is plan gating. Different calls, coaching programs, and content types are restricted to specific membership tiers. FF Theory and FF Hot Seats are Fast Forward only. Private coaching program Hot Seats are restricted to members of that specific program. Pro members see different content than Free members.

If a member expects to have access and doesn't, the next step is to check their current plan in their account settings, then contact NHB support if the issue persists.

docs.title: A member is having a technical problem — how do they get help?
docs.text: Members can contact NHB support through the platform's help or support channel. For coaching program issues, members can also post in the coaching program's Discord channel or reach out through the forum.

docs.title: How does a member update their payment information?
docs.text: Members can update their payment information through their account settings on the NHB platform, or directly through ThriveCart at grow.thrivecart.com/updateinfo/.

docs.title: How does a member reset their password?
docs.text: Password reset is available at app.nothingheldback.com/auth?view=reset. Members enter the email associated with their NHB account and receive a reset link.

docs.title: Does NHB provide transcripts of calls?
docs.text: Yes. Most live calls include a transcript in the Library alongside the video and audio recording. This makes it easier for members to search for specific moments or quickly scan a call without watching the full video.

docs.title: What kind of results can a member expect?
docs.text:
NHB does not make predictions about specific member results. Outcomes depend on the member's effort, their market, their offer, their starting point, and many variables outside of what NHB or any coach can control. What NHB provides is the training, coaching, feedback, tools, and environment designed to help members develop stronger skills and make better decisions. What members do with that is up to them.

This is covered in detail in the NHB income and results policy.

docs.title: Does NHB make income claims?
docs.text: No. NHB does not promise any specific income, revenue, or business outcome. Past results by coaches or other members are not representative of what any individual member will achieve. See the NHB income and results policy.

docs.title: How does NHB talk about competitors?
docs.text: NHB does not comment negatively on other companies, platforms, communities, or public figures. When asked about a competitor, NHB focuses on its own approach rather than characterizing others. See the NHB competitor policy.

docs.title: Is NHB suitable for beginners?
docs.text:
NHB includes members at every stage — from new builders launching their first offer to nine-figure operators scaling established businesses. Some courses, coaching programs, and content are specifically designed for beginners, while others assume significant existing experience.

The best way for a new member to evaluate fit is to attend a few live calls, browse the Library, and see whether the teaching matches what they are trying to learn. For members who want structured guidance from day one, a coaching program provides that — the coach can meet the member where they are and build from there.

docs.title: Can members share NHB content publicly?
docs.text: NHB content is for NHB members. Members should not share recorded calls, course content, or member-submitted work publicly. Sharing outside of NHB undermines the community and can result in membership termination. Swipe files, templates, and resources shared inside NHB are for the member's own use and adaptation, not for public redistribution.

docs.title: Does NHB have an affiliate or referral program?
docs.text: NHB may offer referral or partner programs at various points. Members interested in referring others should check the current status through NHB support or the platform's partner program section.

docs.title: How does a member report a problem with another member's behavior?
docs.text: The NHB platform has a built-in report system. Members can report posts, comments, or users directly through the three-dot menu on any content. Reports go to NHB admins for review.

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks a general question about NHB that doesn't fit cleanly into a single feature or coach doc, this FAQ covers the most common patterns. For specific features (Fast Feedback, Hot Seats, Forum, and so on), refer to the dedicated feature document. For coaching programs, refer to the coaching-programs document or the individual coach document. For pricing and plans, refer to the plans-and-pricing document.

Coaching Program — specialty add-ons on top of NHB Pro or Fast Forward. Each program is $1,000 per month. Each coaching program is led by one coach focused on one discipline.

docs.title: Coaching programs
docs.text:
Meta Ads & Scale Lab (MASL) — coaching program led by Loren Pinilis, focused on Facebook and Instagram advertising.

Google Ads & Scaling Lab (GASL) — coaching program led by Charles Kirkland, focused on Google Ads and paid traffic scaling.

Live Launch (LL) — coaching program led by Kevin Sheerin, focused on offer construction, product-market fit, and low-to-mid-ticket launches.

CRO Accelerator (CROA) — coaching program led by Brandon Vasquez, focused on conversion rate optimization.

Email to CMO Pro — coaching program led by Isaac Lara, focused on email marketing and the path from marketer to CMO.

Copywriting Mastery — coaching program led by Chris Haddad, focused on direct response copywriting, VSLs, and emotional storytelling.

AI Superpower — coaching program led by Robert Neckelius, focused on AI systems for marketing and business.

docs.title: Platform features
docs.text:
Fast Feedback (FF) — asynchronous personalized feedback from a coach. Members submit work via Google Doc, coach responds with a Loom video (typically). Note: "FF" can refer to either Fast Feedback or Fast Forward depending on context — always disambiguate from context.

Hot Seat — a live call format where a member's business, offer, or question is worked on in real time by a coach in front of the community. Members submit context via Google Doc and the coach discusses it on the scheduled call.

Live Call / Live Calls — scheduled Zoom sessions hosted by Alen, the coaching team, and guest speakers. All live calls are recorded.

NHB Theory — Alen's weekly deep-teaching call for NHB Pro members. Covers core NHB marketing and business thinking.

FF Theory — Alen's weekly deep-teaching call for Fast Forward members only. Goes deeper than NHB Theory into mastery-level material.

FF Hot Seats — Alen's weekly Hot Seat call for Fast Forward members only.

NHB Coaching Call — the umbrella term for each coach's weekly training call on their specialty (Meta Ads Scale Lab, Google Ads & Scaling Lab, and so on).

Monthly NHB Pro Hot Seat — each coach runs one per month. Replaces their regular weekly call that week. Open to any NHB Pro member who books a slot.

Library — searchable archive of every past call, Hot Seat, Fast Feedback response, course, and piece of long-form content produced inside NHB.

Library of Truth Trainings — each coach's curated set of trainings inside their coaching program's member vault. The name is the coach's own branding (Charles uses it, Brandon uses it, Loren uses it, others).

Insights — written articles and long-form content inside NHB.

Resources — practical assets like templates, swipe files, tools, and references. Separate from courses and live calls.

Swipe files — example ad creative, landing pages, sales letters, emails, and other copy assets members can reference and adapt. Alen's swipe stash is part of NHB's resources.

Courses — structured, step-by-step learning programs. Each coach has their own course curriculum inside their coaching program.

Playlists — curated ordered sequences of content pulled from the Library, organized around a specific learning path.

Meetups — in-person and virtual gatherings organized by NHB members and coaches.

Forum — NHB's native, long-form, searchable community discussion space on the platform.

Discord — NHB's live chat layer, running on the Discord platform. For real-time community conversation.

Rolodex — the searchable member directory inside the Connect section of NHB.

MindAI — the AI assistant built into NHB, trained on NHB content. Helps members find answers, navigate the library, and understand concepts.

Bookmarks — saved references to content inside NHB. Private to the member.

Public Profile — each member's profile page, visible to other members, showing bio, work, links, coaching programs, and activity.

Home Dashboard — the main landing page members see when they log into NHB.

NHB Retreat — NHB's flagship in-person experience, a separate offering from the membership and coaching programs.

docs.title: Teaching concepts and frameworks
docs.text:
Socratic method — NHB's core teaching approach. Teaches members how to think rather than handing out step-by-step systems, templates, or fill-in-the-blank formulas. Used by Alen and throughout NHB.

P.I.G. Method (Punched In The Gut) — Chris Haddad's signature copywriting framework. Focuses on deep empathy, psychological insight, and narrative technique to create copy that produces visceral emotional response.

Compression Pricing — Alen's term for pricing structures designed to filter for committed members. The Fast Forward down-payment structure is an example — the down payment filters for members who will stay long enough to get real value.

Media Buyer's Media Buyer — Charles Kirkland's industry nickname, reflecting his role as a media buyer who teaches other media buyers.

Plan Subscription — the data type used internally for member plan-level subscriptions (was formerly called "User Current Subscription" or "Current User Subscription" before being renamed).

Coaching Subscription — the data type used internally for coaching program subscriptions (was formerly called "CoachingSubscription").

Subscription Source — the field that tags subscription records as TC (ThriveCart), IS (InfusionSoft), or Manual depending on billing origin.

docs.title: Billing terminology
docs.text:
TC — ThriveCart. One of the two billing paths NHB uses. Legacy member subscriptions often run through ThriveCart.

IS — InfusionSoft. The primary billing path for most new member subscriptions, via NHB's custom IS API built by Umair.

End of Cycle (EOC) — when downgrades and cancellations take effect. Upgrades are immediate; downgrades are processed at the end of the current billing period.

docs.title: Organizational terminology
docs.text:
NHB — Nothing Held Back. The community and platform.

AlphaFour — Alen's company that operates NHB.

NHB Mostar (NHBTEAM) — the active internal team used for project management (Linear tickets).

docs.title: Content type terminology
docs.text:
Post — the universal library-facing record for any piece of content (live call, Hot Seat, Fast Feedback, forum thread, and more). Internal to NHB's data model.

Access Level — how a specific piece of content is gated by membership tier (Free, Pro, Fast Forward).

Required Plan — the minimum plan needed to access a specific piece of content.

docs.title: NHB Plans and Pricing
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB plans and pricing document Applies to: Any question about NHB membership plans, pricing, what's included in each tier, upgrading, downgrading, add-ons, team members, coaching program pricing Last updated: April 2026 (current ThriveCart pricing)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
NHB's membership structure has three tiers and a set of add-on coaching programs. Plus is no longer offered. The current plan hierarchy is:

  • Free (NHB) — free-tier access with limited features
  • NHB Pro — the core paid membership
  • Fast Forward — NHB's flagship mastermind with direct access to Alen

On top of Pro, members can add any of seven specialty coaching programs for direct weekly access to a specific coach.

docs.title: Free (NHB)
docs.text:
• Price: Free
  • Access: Limited entry-level access to the NHB platform. Free members can explore the platform but have minimal access to Live Calls, Fast Feedback, Hot Seats, coaching programs, and most premium content.

docs.title: NHB Pro
docs.text:
• Monthly: $500 per month
  • Annual: $4,500 per year (equivalent to nine months, a standing annual discount)
  • Additional team member: $250 per month to add a team member to an existing NHB Pro seat

What's included:

  • Full access to NHB's content library, trainings, and courses
  • Weekly NHB Theory call with Alen (Thursday 11am EST)
  • Weekly NHB Coaching Calls with each coach on their specialty
  • Monthly NHB Pro Hot Seat calls (rotating across the full coaching team)
  • Monthly Fast Feedback (1 submission per coach per calendar month, any coach except Alen)
  • Access to the full NHB community, Forum, Discord, and Meetups
  • MindAI access
  • Access to all tools, templates, and resources at the Pro tier

docs.title: Fast Forward
docs.text:
Fast Forward is NHB's flagship mastermind program where members work directly with Alen on a hands-on basis. Fast Forward is a step above Pro, not an add-on.

Pricing options:

  • Monthly: $1,000 per month with a $10,000 down payment to start
  • Annual (pay in full): $20,000 per year
  • Annual renewal (existing members): $12,000 per year, or $1,000 per month
  • Additional team member: separate Additional FF Member add-on available
  • FF Pause Plan: available for members who need to temporarily pause their Fast Forward membership

The down payment structure is called "compression pricing" and is designed to filter for members who are committed to staying long enough to get real value from working with Alen.

What's included:

  • Everything in NHB Pro, plus
  • FF Theory call with Alen (Friday 11am EST) — Fast Forward members only
  • FF Hot Seats with Alen (Tuesday 11am EST) — Fast Forward members only
  • Unlimited Fast Feedback submissions to Alen as assigned coach
  • Hands-on strategic work from Alen on the member's offers, funnels, copy, and scaling
  • Direct access to the Fast Forward community within NHB

docs.title: Coaching Programs (add-ons)
docs.text:
Coaching programs are $1,000 per month each, as add-ons on top of an active NHB Pro or Fast Forward membership. A member can add one or more coaching programs.

The seven coaching programs available as add-ons:

Coach Program Monthly price Loren Pinilis Meta Ads & Scale Lab $1,000 Charles Kirkland Google Ads & Scaling Lab $1,000 Kevin Sheerin Live Launch $1,000 Brandon Vasquez CRO Accelerator $1,000 Isaac Lara Email to CMO Pro $1,000 Chris Haddad Copywriting Mastery $1,000 Robert Neckelius AI Superpower $1,000

Fast Forward is the flagship program and is priced separately (see above).

Team member add-ons for coaching programs (MASL, GASL, LL): additional team-member seats available per program. Specific pricing on request via ThriveCart.

What's included in every coaching program:

  • Weekly coaching call with the specific coach
  • Weekly private Hot Seats for program members
  • Fast Feedback twice per week for program members
  • Private community for program members
  • Full coach library of past calls, Fast Feedback, and trainings
  • Access to the coach's complete course curriculum

Members can stack multiple coaching programs when they need depth in more than one area.

docs.title: What is no longer offered
docs.text: • Plus — the legacy Plus tier has been eliminated. The plan hierarchy is Free → Pro → Fast Forward.

docs.title: Upgrades and downgrades
docs.text:
Upgrading (Free → Pro, Pro → FF, or adding a coaching program) takes effect immediately.

Downgrading is processed at the End of Cycle (EOC). A downgrade request scheduled mid-cycle does not take effect until the current billing period ends, so the member retains access to what they paid for until then.

When a member downgrades their base membership to Free, all coaching program add-ons automatically cancel since coaching programs require an active Pro or FF membership.

docs.title: Billing
docs.text: NHB billing infrastructure supports both ThriveCart (TC) and InfusionSoft (IS) paths. Most new member purchases go through IS or ThriveCart via the one-click charge system inside the NHB platform. Members can update their payment information from their account settings.

docs.title: Refund policy
docs.text: All sales are final. No refunds on coaching programs or memberships. If a program or plan is not working, members should cancel before the next billing cycle. This policy exists because coaching programs require the coach's time and attention from day one.

docs.title: How to sign up
docs.text: NHB uses ThriveCart and Stripe for checkout. Sign-up links are provided on the NHB pricing page, inside the platform, and directly via checkout links for each program. Members sign up once at the base membership level (Pro or FF), then add coaching programs separately as add-ons.

docs.title: Team members
docs.text:
Members with multiple team members inside NHB can add additional seats:

  • NHB Pro team member: $250 per month per additional team member
  • Fast Forward team member: separate add-on available
  • Coaching program team members: available for specific programs (MASL, GASL, LL)

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about plans and pricing, the answer should cover:

  • The three tiers: Free (free), NHB Pro ($500/mo or $4,500/yr), Fast Forward ($1k/mo + $10k down or $20k/yr)
  • Existing FF members renew at $12k/yr or $1k/mo
  • Coaching programs are $1,000 per month each, add-ons on top of Pro or FF
  • A member needs an active Pro or FF membership to have any coaching program
  • NHB does not offer the Plus tier anymore — the hierarchy is Free, Pro, Fast Forward
  • Upgrades take effect immediately, downgrades take effect at the end of the billing cycle
  • No refunds; cancel before the next billing cycle
  • Additional team members are available as add-ons on Pro, FF, and select coaching programs

Any questions about whether NHB's pricing is "worth it" or how it compares to other platforms should follow the NHB competitor policy (no comparisons, redirect to what NHB provides) and the NHB income and results policy (no promises about ROI or member outcomes).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: NHB support exists to help members with billing, account, platform, and access issues. For teaching-related questions, coaches inside NHB are accessed through the platform's coaching system rather than direct support. This document is the quick reference for "who do I contact for X."

docs.title: Contacting NHB support
docs.text:
For account, billing, platform, technical, and access questions, NHB support is the primary contact.

  • Email: support@nhbnotify.com (used for platform notifications; also a functional support address)
  • Platform support channel: Members can reach support directly through the NHB platform's support or help section
  • Response times: NHB aims to respond within one business day during normal operating hours

Contact NHB support for:

  • Problems with specific features (calls not loading, content not accessible, technical errors)

docs.title: Contacting a coach
docs.text: Coaches inside NHB are accessed primarily through the platform's coaching system, not through direct email. The right path depends on what the member needs:

docs.title: For feedback on work or specific business questions
docs.text:
• Fast Feedback — submit through the /fast-feedback page with a Google Doc link. The coach reviews and responds with a Loom video (typically).
  • Hot Seats — book a Hot Seat slot on the Hot Seats page for live, real-time coach discussion in front of the community.
  • Weekly coaching calls — attend the coach's weekly NHB Coaching Call or program-specific call, where questions can be asked live.

docs.title: For program-specific questions
docs.text: Coaching program members can post in the private coaching program community (inside NHB and Discord) for coach and peer responses.

docs.title: For questions Alen might answer
docs.text: Alen takes questions through Fast Forward (FF members only) and occasionally through NHB Theory calls (NHB Pro members). Alen does not handle general support questions — those go to NHB support.

docs.title: Not a teaching question — don't contact a coach for it
docs.text:
Members should not reach coaches directly for:

  • Account or billing issues (goes to NHB support)
  • Platform access problems (goes to NHB support)
  • Password reset (goes to NHB support or self-service)
  • Cancelling a membership (goes through account settings or NHB support)
  • Community moderation concerns (goes to moderators via the report system)

Coaches are there for teaching and feedback, not for operational support. Using them for operational questions slows down both the coaching and the support paths.

docs.title: Reporting community violations
docs.text:
For issues with other members' behavior or content inside the community:

  • Built-in report system — use the three-dot menu on any post, comment, or user to report content to moderators
  • Moderator review — reports go to NHB admins and moderators for review and action
  • For severe issues — if a member is experiencing harassment, fraud, or other urgent community issues, they can reach out directly to NHB support in addition to filing a report

See the community guidelines document for detail on what constitutes a violation and how moderation works.

docs.title: Contact for partnerships, press, or business matters
docs.text: Members or external parties looking to reach Alen or NHB for business reasons (partnerships, press inquiries, speaking engagements, or consulting engagements with Alen outside of NHB) can contact through NHB's business channels. Alen's direct business contact is alen@alphafour.com, though the typical path for NHB members is through the platform rather than direct email.

docs.title: Contact for technical issues with the platform
docs.text:
If the NHB platform itself is experiencing technical issues (pages not loading, login errors, video playback failures), members can:

  1. Refresh the page and try again
  2. Clear browser cache or try a different browser
  3. Check for status updates on NHB's announcement channels (Discord announcements, platform notifications)
  4. Report the issue to NHB support with specifics — what they were trying to do, what happened, and any error messages

docs.title: Response expectations
docs.text: NHB support aims for a response within one business day during normal operating hours. More complex issues (billing disputes, account restoration) may take longer to fully resolve even after the initial response. Members should send support a clear description of the issue and any relevant account details to speed resolution.

docs.title: Self-service resources
docs.text:
Before contacting support, members can often resolve issues themselves through:

  • MindAI — for questions about how NHB works, what's included, and where to find things
  • Account settings — for password reset, payment updates, plan changes
  • This knowledge base — for detailed information on policies, features, and processes

If self-service doesn't resolve the issue, contacting support is the right next step.

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks how to get help, the answer should cover:

  • For account, billing, platform issues: NHB support at support@nhbnotify.com or through the platform
  • For feedback on work: Fast Feedback (async) or Hot Seats (live) through the platform
  • For coaching questions: attend the coach's weekly call, submit Fast Feedback, or book a Hot Seat
  • For platform technical issues: NHB support with a specific description of what went wrong
  • For reporting community violations: the built-in report system via the three-dot menu on any content

  • For payment updates: account settings or grow.thrivecart.com/updateinfo/
