docs.title: Brandon Vasquez: CRO Accelerator Coach
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB coach bio document NHB program: CRO Accelerator Applies to: Any question about Brandon Vasquez, his background, his career, his conversion rate optimization work, his teaching, or his role inside Nothing Held Back Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Brandon Vasquez is a full-funnel CRO strategist and revenue optimizer who leads the CRO Accelerator coaching program inside Nothing Held Back. He describes himself as relentlessly data-driven since day one, with a focus on turning raw buyer behavior into repeatable, predictable revenue. Today Brandon manages more than $50 million in annual CRO-driven revenue and builds optimization systems for brands spending up to $50,000 per day on paid traffic.

His specialty is diagnosing and optimizing every stage of a marketing funnel, from the initial click through backend and upsells, so that businesses extract more revenue from the traffic they are already driving rather than relying on more ad spend.

docs.title: Background and early career
docs.text:
Brandon's path into marketing started at the University of Texas at Austin, where he earned a degree in advertising and developed an obsession with influence, human behavior, and what actually drives action. He went deep on persuasion, media, and PR coursework during his time there.

Alongside his academic training, his real education in "people handling" came from managing a restaurant, where he engaged daily with people from every background and learned to quickly read what drives decisions. That instinct became the foundation of his later work as a marketer.

After graduating, Brandon jumped into copywriting and built his portfolio through freelance work on Upwork and Fiverr. That early experience led to a full-time role at a digital ad agency, where he wrote ad copy for major accounts, authority figures, and thought leaders with large audiences across coaching, consulting, and education. Several of his campaigns became the control — the benchmark that other versions had to beat — for launches that reached millions of people.

Copywriting was his entry point into the industry, but he quickly wanted to influence more than just the copy on a page. He wanted to shape the entire customer journey, from the first click through upsells and high-ticket backend offers. That ambition pushed him into conversion rate optimization, where he could refine every stage of the funnel, maximize the impact of every advertising dollar, and turn more leads into long-term customers.

docs.title: Major roles and results
docs.text:
Brandon's career since then has included:

  • Copy Chief and Head of CRO at one of the largest brands in online art education, where he drove seven-figure lifts by optimizing funnels, storefronts, and email strategies
  • Consulting for industry leaders in e-commerce, direct-to-consumer, SaaS, and lead generation in the finance space — taking on crowded and brutally competitive markets
  • Currently managing $50M+ in annual CRO-driven revenue across multiple accounts
  • Building optimization systems for brands spending up to $50,000 per day on ads

He positions his own work as being a "data detective" — cracking the code behind buyer behavior and turning every insight into repeatable profit.

docs.title: What Brandon teaches
docs.text:
Inside the CRO Accelerator program, Brandon's teaching covers the full stack of conversion optimization. His approach is to maximize the value of every click, visit, and customer, so members get more revenue from the traffic they are already driving rather than having to buy more.

Core focus areas:

  • Maximizing the value of every click, visit, and customer
  • Structuring split tests around what actually moves the needle — offer, layout, messaging, and user flow — not surface-level tweaks
  • Building reliable systems that improve conversions, increase average order value (AOV), and make funnels perform rather than just look good

Library of Truth Trainings (available inside the CRO Accelerator member vault):

  • Anatomy of High-Converting Landing Pages — what actually makes a landing page perform and what is just noise
  • Market Voice to Market Fit — matching messaging to what an audience actually wants to hear
  • The CRO Audit & Roadmap Playbook — a step-by-step process for auditing funnels and building a prioritized testing roadmap
  • Heatmap Mastery — uncovering hidden user behaviors and bottlenecks through heatmap analysis
  • Competition Researcher Decoder — how to read competitor funnels, positioning, and traffic to find gaps and opportunities

Upcoming trainings in development:

  • Page Friction Fixers — eliminating the hidden points of resistance that cost conversions
  • Retention Rocket Fuel — strategies that keep customers buying and coming back
  • Scrollmap Secrets — reading scrollmaps for deeper user insight and smarter page optimization
  • Above-the-Fold Gold — what belongs above the fold to hook, hold, and convert
  • AOV Boosters — tactics to increase average order value without killing conversion rate

Course progression inside CRO Accelerator:

  • CRO Fundamentals — master the basics and set a funnel up for higher conversions
  • CRO Momentum — tactics and strategies that accelerate growth and stack quick, compounding wins
  • CRO Scaling — advanced strategies that break plateaus and drive sustainable, systemized growth at scale
  • CRO Mastery — the art and science of relentless optimization, building growth engines that outperform and outlast the competition

docs.title: Teaching philosophy
docs.text:
Brandon's philosophy is that when the numbers are understood, luck becomes irrelevant. In his own words: "When you know the numbers, you don't need luck. You just need a plan."

His core principles:

  • Full-funnel perspective. Every step from the first click to the upsell sequence matters. No single stage is too small to test and optimize.
  • Data as the foundation. Decisions come from disciplined split testing and buyer behavior analysis, not from guessing or from what other people say is working.
  • Structure tests around what moves the needle. Offer, layout, messaging, and user flow are where the real lifts live — not the color of a button.
  • Scalable and repeatable. The goal is systems where scalability and ROI are both predictable and repeatable, not one-off wins.
  • Audience-first thinking. Matching market voice to market fit — building detailed customer understanding before writing copy or designing flows — ensures alignment between message and buyer.

docs.title: Voice
docs.text:
Brandon's voice as a teacher is direct, grounded in numbers, and pragmatic:

"For me, it's about being a data detective and cracking the code behind buyer behavior so I can turn every insight into profit on repeat."

"When you know the numbers, you don't need luck. You just need a plan."

"If you want to improve results without spending more on traffic, I'll show you how to turn underperforming funnels into scalable, high-revenue systems."

docs.title: CRO Accelerator — program curriculum
docs.text:
Positioning: Turn data into revenue with weekly CRO coaching from Brandon Vasquez.

Inside CRO Accelerator, members learn to:

  • Uncover hidden revenue in their existing funnel
  • Run split tests that actually move the needle
  • Lower their CPA while scaling revenue
  • Build data-backed testing strategies
  • Troubleshoot revenue bottlenecks fast

Pricing: $1,000 per month as an add-on to an active NHB Pro or Fast Forward membership.

docs.title: Summary for answering questions about Brandon
docs.text:
When a member asks about Brandon, the answer should describe:

  • What he does: leads NHB's CRO Accelerator program, currently manages $50M+ in annual CRO-driven revenue, and builds optimization systems for brands spending up to $50K per day on ads
  • Background: University of Texas at Austin (Advertising), restaurant management, freelance copywriting on Upwork and Fiverr, full-time copy role at a digital ad agency with campaigns that became controls, then Copy Chief and Head of CRO at one of the largest online art education brands, then consulting across e-commerce, DTC, SaaS, and finance lead gen
  • What he teaches: full-funnel CRO, including landing page anatomy, message-market fit, heatmap and scrollmap analysis, AOV optimization, competitive research, and a course progression from Fundamentals through Mastery
  • Teaching philosophy: data-driven over opinion-driven, full-funnel over single-stage, structured testing on what actually moves the needle, and building repeatable systems rather than chasing one-off wins
  • How he works inside NHB: weekly CRO Adventures training call, weekly CROA Hot Seats for program members, monthly NHB Pro Hot Seat, monthly Fast Feedback, and the Library of Truth Trainings inside the program's member vault

Do not confuse this Brandon Vasquez (the CRO specialist) with other people sharing the name, including the professional soccer player or other public figures. Reference him as "Brandon Vasquez, NHB CRO coach" when ambiguity could arise.

His signature framework, the P.I.G. Method (Punched In The Gut), is a distinctive approach to direct response copywriting built on deep empathy, psychological insight, and narrative technique. The method is designed to produce copy that creates visceral emotional responses in the reader and drives conversions without relying on rational arguments or technical tricks.

docs.title: Career highlights

Chris is also the founder and CEO of Digital Romance, Inc., an eight-figure direct response relationship advice business he built under the commercial pen name Michael Fiore. Operating offers under a separate persona is a legitimate direct response business practice and has been part of Chris's work for many years.

Chris's early mentors in direct response included Harlan Kilstein and the copywriting legend John Carlton, both of whom accelerated his mastery in the craft.

docs.title: Teaching philosophy

Chris's core teaching principle is deep empathy. Stories, in his framing, are the operating system of the human mind, and effective copy works by identifying the anxiety, agony, and wonder beneath a prospect's surface desires and building a narrative that positions the solution as inevitable.

His approach is grounded in decades of battle-tested campaigns rather than theory. Every framework he teaches has been validated on real offers producing real revenue.

Alongside all of that, Isaac raised his younger sister and took in three rescue dogs, including his special-needs sidekick Tuna. His calm-under-pressure approach to marketing grew out of a life that regularly required it in other areas too.

docs.title: Background and early career
docs.text:
Loren began his career in traditional marketing and public relations in 2006, handling the full spread of agency-side work: press releases, print design, radio and TV commercial production, social media, website design, and everything in between.

In 2016, he partnered with a friend to build an online fitness business. In that business he personally handled product creation, producing a podcast, funnel design and building, technology integration, copywriting, email marketing, and paid traffic. That hands-on role across the full stack of a direct response business is where his love for Meta ads began.

From there, Loren dove into Meta ads and landed agency work, where he had the opportunity to work with and learn from some of the most respected agency owners in direct response. That led to opportunities most Meta ad specialists only read about — including producing control-beating Facebook ad copy for Agora Financial.

Rather than chasing the gigs that paid the most, Loren has since deliberately chased the ones that were the most unusual, the most challenging, and the ones that produced the most new learning. The result is that he has worked — and had success — in nearly every niche, every funnel type, and every budget level.

docs.title: What Loren does best

What he does best is look at all the variables — the offer, the budget level, the business, the niche, the ad account history — and turn that into a Meta ads system that actually produces results for that specific situation.

Four specific skill areas anchor his work:

  • Discord — real-time chat. For daily conversation, quick questions, live-call reactions, and casual community presence.

  • NHB Pro members with a Coaching Program subscription — get an additional 2 submissions per week to their program coach (separate from and on top of the Pro monthly quota)
  • NHB Free (NHB) members — no access to Fast Feedback
  • Plus members (legacy tier, no longer offered) — historically had no submission access

Alen is available as a coach for Fast Forward members only. Pro members who want access to Alen's feedback see an upgrade prompt inviting them to join Fast Forward.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The submission flow for current Fast Feedback uses Google Docs rather than a long in-app form. A member:

  1. Goes to the /fast-feedback page and clicks Get Feedback.
  2. Selects the coach they want feedback from (Fast Forward members are pre-assigned Alen).
  3. Provides a Google Doc link containing their question, context, and whatever work they want reviewed.
  4. Chooses whether the submission should be Public (visible to all Fast Forward members in the feed) or Private (only visible to the member and their coach).
  5. Submits.

The coach then reviews the Google Doc on their own schedule and records a response. The recommended response format is a Loom video — the reply input on the coach side is explicitly labeled "Most coaches reply with video." Coaches can also leave text notes when useful.

When the coach submits their response, the member receives both an in-app notification and an email with the subject "Fast Feedback reply."

docs.title: Submission quotas
docs.text:
Fast Forward members have no submission limit. They submit to Alen as often as they want.

NHB Pro members are limited to 1 submission per coach per calendar month. The quota resets at the start of each new calendar month. If a member has already submitted to Coach X this month, the submit button for Coach X is disabled with a message showing "You've reached your monthly submission limit to [Coach]." The member can still submit to other coaches that same month.

NHB Pro + Coaching Program members get a separate 2 submissions per week quota to their program coach, calculated Monday through Sunday. This is independent from the monthly Pro quota — submissions to the program coach count only against the weekly program quota, and submissions to other coaches count only against the monthly Pro quota.

docs.title: Public vs Private submissions
docs.text:
When submitting, members choose Public or Private:

  • Public — the submission and the coach's response are visible to all Fast Forward members in the shared Fast Feedback feed. Other members can learn from the review.
  • Private — only the submitter and the assigned coach can see the submission and response. Useful for sensitive business details.

Private submissions do not appear in the public feed. The content is protected by privacy rules at the data layer, not just hidden in the interface.

docs.title: The Fast Feedback feed
docs.text:
Fast Forward and Pro members can browse the public Fast Feedback feed on the /fast-feedback page. The feed has five tabs:

  • Discover — every public submission across the entire community
  • Search — full-text search across indexed submissions
  • Bookmarked — submissions the member has saved to come back to
  • Unread — public submissions the member has not yet opened
  • My Fast Feedback — the member's own submissions, both public and private

Members can filter the feed by coach and by category, and use pagination to browse through older submissions.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text:
• Main page — /fast-feedback on the NHB platform
  • Navigation — look for Fast Feedback in the main NHB sidebar

Coaches access the admin side of Fast Feedback through the admin panel, which is not visible to regular members.

docs.title: Related features
docs.text:
• Hot Seats — live call version of personalized coach feedback, where a member's work is discussed in real time in front of the community. Complements Fast Feedback, which is asynchronous.
  • Coaching Programs — members enrolled in a program get additional FF quota with their program coach beyond the base Pro allocation.
  • Forum — members can also share work and get peer feedback in the forum, though the forum is peer-to-peer, not coach-delivered.

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about Fast Feedback, the answer should cover:

  • What it is: direct coach feedback on the member's work, usually as a Loom video response
  • Who has access: Fast Forward (unlimited, Alen), Pro (1/coach/month, any coach except Alen), Pro + Coaching Program (additional 2/week to program coach)
  • How to submit: Google Doc link on /fast-feedback, select coach, choose Public or Private
  • How coaches respond: typically a Loom video, delivered when the coach reviews the doc
  • When it arrives: no guaranteed turnaround — members get a notification and email when the coach responds
  • How to see others' feedback: the Discover tab on /fast-feedback shows all public submissions

Any questions about how quickly a coach will respond, whether a member will get specific revenue results from applying feedback, or comparison to other platforms' feedback features should follow the NHB income and results policy and competitor policy respectively.

docs.title: Forum
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about the NHB Forum — what it is, how to post, category access, moderation, tagging members, how it differs from Discord Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The NHB Forum is the community discussion space inside the NHB platform. It is where members post questions, share wins, discuss what they are building, get peer input, and connect with coaches and other operators in long-form threaded conversations.

Unlike a chat channel (which scrolls past and disappears), the forum is organized, searchable, and durable. A thread started today can be found, read, and replied to a year from now. This is where the most substantive community discussion happens inside NHB.

NHB is transitioning member-to-member discussion onto the platform's own forum over time. The legacy Facebook group still exists during the transition, and Discord remains in place for live, real-time chat. The forum is the long-form community home.

docs.title: How the Forum is organized
docs.text:
The forum is divided into categories, each focused on a specific topic or program area. Members browse by category, or use the main feed to see the most recent activity across categories they have access to.

Typical category groupings include:

  • Plan tier lounges — dedicated spaces for members of specific plan tiers
  • Topic categories — threads about specific disciplines (copywriting, ads, CRO, email, offers, funnels, scaling, and more)
  • Coaching program categories — discussion spaces for members of specific coaching programs
  • Fast Feedback categories — forum spaces linked to Fast Feedback submissions
  • Hot Seat categories — threads tied to Hot Seat submissions and post-call discussion

Each category has its own access rules. A category may be open to all paid members, or restricted to a specific plan tier or coaching program.

docs.title: Category access
docs.text:
Forum category access is determined by:

  • Plan tier — some categories are open to all paid members, some are restricted to NHB Pro or above, and some are restricted to Fast Forward members only
  • Coaching Program enrollment — coaching program categories are restricted to members enrolled in that specific program
  • Fast Forward-only categories — marked for Fast Forward members, not visible to other tiers

A member who does not have access to a category will not see it in their category list. The platform only shows categories the current member is allowed to read.

docs.title: Creating a thread
docs.text:
Members can create a new thread from inside any category they have access to. When creating a thread, members:

  1. Choose the category the thread belongs to (from the list of accessible categories)
  2. Write a thread title
  3. Write the thread body — supports formatted text, links, images, and embedded video
  4. Submit

The thread then appears in the category and in the main feed for members with access. New threads typically attract replies from other members, and coaches sometimes jump into threads when the topic is in their area.

docs.title: Replying and engagement
docs.text:
Threads support nested replies. Members can:

  • Reply to the main thread or to a specific comment within the thread
  • Mention other members with @ to tag them and trigger a notification
  • Like threads and comments
  • Bookmark threads to come back to them later
  • Report content that violates NHB's community standards (via the report system)

Threads can be followed so the member gets notifications on new replies.

docs.title: Finding threads
docs.text:
Members can discover forum content in several ways:

  • Recent activity — the main forum feed shows recent threads across accessible categories
  • Category view — browse a specific category's threads
  • Search — full-text search across all accessible forum content (powered by Algolia)
  • Notifications — mentions, replies to the member's threads, and updates on followed threads surface in notifications
  • Bookmarks — saved threads appear in the member's bookmarks

docs.title: Forum versus Discord versus Facebook group
docs.text:
NHB maintains three community spaces, each with a different role:

  • NHB Forum — the platform's native, long-form, searchable community space. The primary home for substantive discussion, durable threads, and community learning.
  • Discord — live chat for real-time conversation. Fast-paced, chatty, less structured. Used for daily back-and-forth, reactions, quick questions, and community bonding.
  • Facebook group — the legacy community space from before the platform had its own forum. Members are being transitioned onto the NHB platform forum over time. The Facebook group still exists but is being phased out.

For anything a member wants to be able to find later, refer back to, or share with specific intent, the NHB Forum is the right space. For quick chat and daily presence, Discord is the right space.

docs.title: Community standards
docs.text: The NHB Forum is moderated. Members are expected to engage respectfully, contribute meaningfully, and support other members' growth. Content that targets or criticizes specific public figures or companies outside NHB, income claims, or anything that violates NHB's community standards may be moderated or removed. Members can report content to admins via the built-in reporting system.

docs.title: Where to find the Forum
docs.text:
• Main platform navigation — Forum is a top-level section in the NHB platform navigation
  • Category sidebar — inside the forum, members see their accessible categories in a sidebar
  • Home dashboard — recent forum activity surfaces in the home feed

docs.title: Related features
docs.text:
• Discord — real-time chat layer (separate platform, connected to NHB community)
  • Bookmarks — save threads to come back to
  • Notifications — get alerted when mentioned, replied to, or when followed threads update
  • Search — full-text search across forum content
  • Hot Seats and Fast Feedback — for personalized coach feedback rather than peer discussion

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about the Forum, the answer should cover:

  • What it is: the NHB platform's long-form, searchable community discussion space
  • How categories work: organized by topic and tier; only accessible categories are visible to the member
  • Access rules: plan tier and coaching program enrollment determine which categories a member can see and post in
  • How to use it: browse categories, create threads, reply, mention, bookmark, follow, search
  • Difference from Discord: forum is durable and searchable, Discord is live chat
  • Difference from Facebook group: Facebook group is legacy and being phased out, NHB platform forum is the home going forward

Any questions about specific NHB members or their business details, or requests to evaluate content against competitor platforms, should follow the NHB income and results policy and competitor policy.

docs.title: Home Dashboard
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about the home page, dashboard, home feed, what members see when they log in Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The Home Dashboard is the first page members see when they log into the NHB platform. It surfaces what's happening now: upcoming live calls, recent Library additions, forum activity, updates from coaches, Fast Feedback responses, Hot Seat bookings, and any platform announcements the member needs to see.

The dashboard is designed so that a member who logs in for five minutes to "check NHB" can get oriented quickly — what's live today, what's new, what needs attention.

docs.title: What appears on the Home Dashboard
docs.text:
The dashboard typically includes:

  • Upcoming live calls — the next few scheduled calls the member has access to, with date, time, host, and the option to attend
  • Recent Library additions — newly added recordings, Fast Feedback responses, and content the member might care about
  • Forum activity — recent threads and discussions in categories the member follows or has access to
  • Coaching updates — messages from coaches, program updates, and coach-specific announcements
  • Personal activity — recent Fast Feedback responses to the member, mentions, and replies to the member's own posts
  • Platform updates — NHB announcements about new features, changes, or important notices
  • Profile completion card — if the member hasn't filled in parts of their profile, a prompt to complete it (cosmetic only, not gated)

Content is surfaced based on the member's plan, coaching program enrollment, followed members, and recent engagement patterns.

docs.title: Color mode
docs.text: Members can switch between dark and light color modes through the account settings. This preference persists across sessions.

docs.title: Where to find the Home Dashboard
docs.text:
• Root URL — the main index page of the NHB platform is the Home Dashboard
  • Home navigation link — clicking "Home" in the main navigation always returns to the Dashboard

docs.title: Related features
docs.text:
• Live Calls — upcoming calls surface first on the Dashboard; full schedule lives on the Live Calls page
  • Library — recent Library additions feed into the Dashboard; full archive is on the Library page
  • Forum — recent forum activity shows on the Dashboard; full forum is on the Forum page
  • Notifications — item-level notifications are separate from Dashboard content but complement it

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about the Home Dashboard, the answer should cover:

  • What it is: the main landing page members see when they log into NHB
  • What appears on it: upcoming live calls, recent Library additions, forum activity, coaching updates, personal activity, platform announcements
  • How it is personalized: content is filtered by the member's plan, coaching program, followed members, and recent activity
  • Color mode toggle: dark or light mode, configurable in settings
  • Where to get to it: the Home link in the main platform navigation, or the root of the NHB platform

docs.title: Hot Seats
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about Hot Seats — what they are, how to submit, who runs them, scheduling, how submissions become live call discussions Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Hot Seats are live calls where a member's business, offer, or question gets worked on in real time by a coach in front of the NHB community. A member submits their context ahead of time through a Google Doc, and the coach picks it up and discusses it on the scheduled call.

There is no review or approval gate — the submission is the input, the live discussion is the output. Members see coaches working through real businesses every week, which is often more educational than hearing the same concepts taught in the abstract.

docs.title: How Hot Seats work
docs.text:
1. A member finds an upcoming Hot Seat slot on the Hot Seats page and clicks Book a Hot Seat.
  2. They fill out the submission popup with a Google Doc link that contains their business context, question, and any material they want the coach to look at.
  3. The submission is booked to that specific upcoming call.
  4. On the call, the coach opens the Google Doc and works through it live with the member and the community.

Only Google Doc links are accepted for submissions. The platform validates this and will show an error if another link type is used.

docs.title: Types of Hot Seats inside NHB
docs.text:
The NHB platform runs three categories of Hot Seats, each tied to a different program:

  • Fast Forward Hot Seats — hosted by Alen, available to Fast Forward members. Members submit through the Fast Feedback section of the platform.
  • NHB Pro Hot Seats — once per month, each coach runs a dedicated NHB Pro Hot Seat call where any Pro member can request to be in the hot seat. These replace the coach's regular weekly training call that week.
  • Coaching Program Hot Seats — each coach runs a weekly private Hot Seat session for members of their specific coaching program. These are restricted to members enrolled in that program.

The Coaching Program Hot Seats include:

  • MASL Hot Seats — hosted by Loren Pinilis for Meta Ads & Scale Lab members
  • GASL Hot Seats — hosted by Charles Kirkland for Google Ads & Scaling Lab members
  • AI Superpower Hot Seats — hosted by Robert Neckelius for AI Superpower members
  • Copywriting Mastery Hot Seats — hosted by Chris Haddad for Copywriting Mastery members
  • LL Hot Seats — hosted by Kevin Sheerin for Live Launch members
  • Email to CMO Pro Hot Seats — hosted by Isaac Lara for Email to CMO Pro members
  • CROA Hot Seats — hosted by Brandon Vasquez for CRO Accelerator members

docs.title: Finding and booking Hot Seats
docs.text:
The Hot Seats page shows upcoming sessions in a grouped feed:

  • This Week — sessions happening in the next 7 days
  • Next Week — sessions 8 to 14 days out
  • Upcoming — sessions beyond 14 days, expandable with Load More

Each card shows the date, the hosting coach, and a button to book or view attendance.

Past Hot Seats do not appear on the upcoming feed. Recordings of past Hot Seats live in the NHB Library, where members can search and filter them.

docs.title: Managing a booked Hot Seat
docs.text:
Once a member has booked a Hot Seat, they see a Booked Actions panel on the call card with four options:

  • View GDoc — opens the submitted Google Doc in a new tab
  • Edit Submission — reopens the submission popup to update the doc link or details
  • Reschedule — moves the submission to a different upcoming call (multi-step popup)
  • Cancel — cancels the booking

docs.title: Who can submit Hot Seats
docs.text:
Access to submitting a Hot Seat depends on membership level and program enrollment:

  • Fast Forward Hot Seats — Fast Forward members only
  • Coaching Program Hot Seats — members enrolled in the specific coaching program only (for example, CRO Accelerator Hot Seats are restricted to CRO Accelerator members)
  • NHB Pro Hot Seats — any NHB Pro member, typically monthly per coach

Free and Plus members (legacy) do not have Hot Seat submission access.

docs.title: The submission form
docs.text:
The Hot Seat submission form (pop.ApplyHotSeat) is a short multi-step popup. The member:

  1. Chooses which upcoming session to submit to (sessions with open slots)
  2. Reviews the submission rules
  3. Selects whether the submission is a Question (specific business question) or a Review (full business/offer review)
  4. Provides the Google Doc link with their context and material
  5. Confirms and submits

The popup closes on a success screen once the submission is locked in.

docs.title: Where to find Hot Seats
docs.text:
• Main page — the Hot Seats section on the NHB platform
  • Library — past Hot Seat recordings are stored in the NHB Library for on-demand replay
  • Fast Feedback page — Fast Forward Hot Seats submit through the Fast Feedback section

docs.title: Related features
docs.text:
• Fast Feedback — asynchronous version of personalized coach feedback, via Loom video rather than live discussion
  • Live Calls — regular training calls run by each coach; Hot Seats are one format within the broader live call schedule
  • Coaching Programs — each coaching program includes its own weekly Hot Seat, available only to program members

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about Hot Seats, the answer should cover:

  • What they are: live calls where a coach works through a member's business, offer, or question in real time in front of the community
  • Who can submit: Fast Forward members (FF Hot Seats with Alen), coaching program members (their program's Hot Seat), and NHB Pro members (monthly Pro Hot Seat with each coach)
  • How to submit: Google Doc link via the submission popup on the Hot Seats page
  • How scheduling works: members book a specific upcoming session, then the coach picks up the submission and discusses it on that call
  • How to manage a booking: View GDoc, Edit, Reschedule, or Cancel from the booked call card
  • Where to watch past Hot Seats: the NHB Library has all recordings

Any questions about outcomes a member will get from being in a Hot Seat, specific revenue claims, or comparisons to other communities' Hot Seat formats should follow the NHB income and results policy and competitor policy.

docs.title: Library
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about the NHB Library, finding past calls, accessing recordings, searching content, accessing coach archives Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The NHB Library is the searchable archive of every live call, training, Hot Seat, coaching session, Fast Feedback response, and piece of long-form content produced inside NHB. If a member has ever wondered "what did Alen say about X on that call" or "where is Loren's training on creative testing," the Library is where they find it.

The Library is the largest single repository of current direct response teaching inside NHB. Content is organized by coach, topic, content type, and date, and is fully searchable.

docs.title: What's in the Library
docs.text:
• Live call recordings — every past NHB Coaching Call, NHB Theory call, FF Theory call, FF Hot Seat, guest call, and coaching program session
  • Hot Seat replays — past Hot Seat calls where coaches worked through member businesses
  • Fast Feedback responses — past public Fast Feedback submissions and coach responses
  • Courses — course lessons and structured learning content
  • Insights — written articles and long-form breakdowns
  • Playlists — curated sequences of content grouped for specific learning paths
  • Resources — templates, swipe files, and downloadable assets linked to content

Each entry typically includes the video recording, an audio-only version, a transcript, summaries (short and long form where prepared), and any supporting Google Docs or resources shared during the session.

docs.title: How content is organized
docs.text:
Members can browse the Library in several ways:

  • By coach — filter to see all content from a specific coach (Alen, Chris, Charles, Loren, Kevin, Brandon, Isaac, Robert)
  • By topic — filter by marketing discipline (copywriting, ads, email, CRO, offers, scaling, and more)
  • By content type — Live Calls, Hot Seats, Fast Feedback, Courses, Insights, Resources
  • By plan tier — only content the member has access to is shown
  • By date — most recent first, or browsed chronologically

docs.title: Search
docs.text: The Library supports full-text search. Members can type a topic, a concept, a name, or a specific question and the search returns matching entries from across the entire Library. Search is powered by Algolia and covers titles, descriptions, summaries, and relevant metadata.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
Library access is tiered:

  • Free members — limited or no access to premium content
  • NHB Pro members — full access to NHB Pro content library, including all NHB Theory calls, NHB Coaching Calls, and most Hot Seats
  • Coaching Program members — Pro library plus the full archive of their specific coaching program (their coach's past calls, Hot Seats, and Fast Feedback)
  • Fast Forward members — full access including FF Theory calls and FF Hot Seats with Alen (FF-exclusive content not available at other tiers)

Some content is gated by additional plan requirements at the individual post level — for example, FF Hot Seats are visible only to Fast Forward members regardless of whether a Pro member has access to the Library generally.

docs.title: Bookmarking and following
docs.text: Members can bookmark any Library entry to come back to it later. Bookmarked items appear in the member's Bookmarks section. Members can also follow specific coaches or topics to get updates when new content is added.

docs.title: Coach libraries (inside coaching programs)
docs.text: Each coaching program member gets access to their coach's complete searchable archive — past Hot Seats, Theory calls, Fast Feedback submissions, and any other material the coach has produced. This is a focused subset of the Library specifically for that coaching program's discipline.

docs.title: Where to find the Library
docs.text:
• Main platform navigation — Library is a top-level section on the NHB platform
  • Home dashboard — recent Library additions surface in the home feed
  • Coach pages — each coach's page shows their content within the Library, filtered to their work

docs.title: Related features
docs.text:
• Search — the Library's search function uses the platform's Algolia-powered search
  • Live Calls — upcoming calls appear in Live Calls; past calls land in the Library after they end
  • Courses — structured learning paths that often overlap with Library content
  • Bookmarks — save Library content to come back to it
  • MindAI — can help members find specific Library content without browsing or searching manually

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about the Library, the answer should cover:

  • What it is: the searchable archive of every past call, training, Hot Seat, Fast Feedback response, course, and piece of content produced inside NHB
  • How to browse: by coach, topic, content type, plan tier, or date
  • Search: full-text search powered by Algolia, covering titles, descriptions, and summaries
  • What's included in each entry: video recording, audio, transcript, summary, attached resources
  • Access: tiered by membership level, with FF-exclusive content visible only to Fast Forward members
  • Where to find it: the Library section of the NHB platform

docs.title: Live Calls
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about live calls, training calls, the call schedule, Zoom links, coach calls, guest calls, or where to find upcoming and past calls Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Live calls are scheduled video sessions hosted by Alen, the coaching team, and guest speakers. They are where most of the real-time teaching inside NHB happens — the place members get new ideas first, work through them together, and connect directly with the coaches.

Every live call runs on Zoom. Every call is recorded. All recordings are stored in the NHB Library and searchable for on-demand replay after the call ends.

docs.title: Monthly NHB Pro Hot Seat rotation
docs.text:
Once every four weeks, each coach's regular weekly training call is replaced by a dedicated Monthly NHB Pro Hot Seat call. On these weeks, NHB Pro members can request to be in the hot seat and work through their business live with that coach. This gives every NHB Pro member access to hot-seat-style coaching from the full coaching team over a rolling monthly cycle.

Alen runs his own Monthly NHB Pro Hot Seat on the first Thursday of each month, replacing the regular NHB Theory call that week.

docs.title: Types of live calls
docs.text:
NHB has several categories of live calls:

  • NHB Coaching Calls — weekly training calls run by each coach on their specialty area. These are the core weekly teaching sessions and are open to NHB Pro members.
  • NHB Theory — Alen's weekly deep-teaching call covering NHB's core marketing and business thinking. Open to NHB Pro members.
  • FF Theory and FF Hot Seats — Alen's dedicated calls for Fast Forward members only, covering tactical and strategic depth at the mastery level.
  • Coaching Program Hot Seats — weekly private Hot Seat sessions for each coaching program. Restricted to members enrolled in that specific program.
  • NHB Pro Hot Seats — monthly rotation where each coach does a dedicated Hot Seat call for NHB Pro members.
  • Guest Calls — appearances from outside experts, practitioners, and top operators sharing what they are seeing in their businesses.

docs.title: Who can attend which calls
docs.text:
Access depends on membership level and coaching program enrollment:

  • Fast Forward members — full access: FF Theory, FF Hot Seats, every NHB Coaching Call, every NHB Theory call, and any coaching program sessions they have subscribed to
  • NHB Pro members — every NHB Coaching Call, NHB Theory, and Monthly NHB Pro Hot Seats. Private Coaching Program Hot Seats require enrollment in that specific coaching program.
  • NHB Pro + Coaching Program members — everything above plus the weekly private Hot Seat for their enrolled program
  • Free (NHB) members — no access to live calls

docs.title: How to attend a live call
docs.text:
Upcoming calls appear in the Live Calls feed on the NHB platform, grouped by time:

  • This Week — calls happening in the next 7 days
  • Next Week — calls 8 to 14 days out
  • Upcoming — calls further out, expandable with Load More

Each call card shows the date, time, host, and an Attend button to add the call to the member's attendance list. Zoom links are shared on the call card or through the platform shortly before the call begins.

When a member marks themselves as attending, they show up in the attendee list on that specific call. Each call has its own Zoom link, which is visible on the call detail page.

docs.title: Call recordings
docs.text:
Every live call is recorded. Recordings typically become available in the NHB Library shortly after the call ends, along with:

  • The Zoom recording (playable in-app)
  • An audio-only version
  • A transcript
  • A summary (short and long form, where prepared)
  • Any Google Doc resources shared during the call

Past live call recordings can be found in the NHB Library, searchable by coach, topic, date, and content type.

docs.title: Where to find Live Calls
docs.text:
• Main page — the Live Calls page on the NHB platform
  • Library — all past call recordings live in the NHB Library for on-demand replay
  • Individual coach pages — each coaching program page also shows the upcoming and past calls for that program
  • Home dashboard — recent and upcoming calls surface in the home feed

docs.title: Related features
docs.text:
• Hot Seats — a specific format of live call where a member's business is worked on in real time
  • Library — archive of all past call recordings
  • Fast Feedback — asynchronous alternative to live coaching, delivered as recorded video feedback

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about live calls, the answer should cover:

  • The weekly schedule by day and time, with host and program
  • Which tier is required to attend each type of call (NHB Pro, Fast Forward, or specific Coaching Program)
  • How to attend: go to the Live Calls page, click into a call, get the Zoom link
  • What happens after: every call is recorded and lands in the Library
  • How Monthly NHB Pro Hot Seats work: each coach runs one per month, replacing their regular weekly call that week
