Any questions comparing NHB's call schedule or coaching cadence to other platforms should follow the NHB competitor policy.

docs.title: Meetups
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about meetups, in-person gatherings, member-organized events Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Meetups are in-person and virtual gatherings organized by NHB members and coaches. They are how the proximity built online becomes real-world connection — dinners, co-working days, mastermind sessions, conferences attended together, and regional meetups organized by members in specific cities.

NHB is a community of operators from many different places, and Meetups are how members take the relationships built in the forum, in Discord, and on Hot Seats offline.

docs.title: Types of Meetups
docs.text:
Meetups inside NHB cover a range of formats:

  • Regional member meetups — dinners, drinks, or co-working sessions organized by members in specific cities and regions
  • Coach-led gatherings — events organized around a specific coach or coaching program
  • Conference and event meetups — NHB members coordinating to attend industry conferences together
  • Retreats and masterminds — higher-intensity gatherings for specific member groups
  • Virtual meetups — Zoom gatherings, virtual workshops, and themed discussions

docs.title: How Meetups work
docs.text:
Members can find upcoming Meetups on the Meetups page of the NHB platform. Each meetup has:

  • A date and location (or Zoom link for virtual meetups)
  • A description of the format and who it's for
  • An attendee list of other members planning to attend
  • An option to RSVP or join

Members can also organize their own meetups by creating a new meetup entry — inviting other NHB members in their city or around a specific topic.

docs.title: Who can attend
docs.text: Meetups are generally open to paying NHB members. Some Meetups are restricted — for example, Fast Forward-only retreats, coaching-program-specific events, or events with capacity limits.

docs.title: Why Meetups matter
docs.text: The environment inside NHB is designed to expose members to the right people. Meetups are how that proximity becomes real — members meet face-to-face, build relationships, sharpen each other in person, and often form partnerships, joint ventures, or ongoing friendships that last beyond the membership.

docs.title: Where to find Meetups
docs.text:
• Main platform navigation — Meetups section on the NHB platform
  • Home dashboard — upcoming Meetups appear in the home feed
  • Community and forum — Meetups are often discussed and coordinated in the forum before they happen

docs.title: Related features
docs.text:
• Forum — where Meetups are often discussed and coordinated
  • Discord — where ongoing member-to-member chat around Meetups often happens
  • Retreat (separate flagship event) — NHB's most immersive in-person experience, distinct from member-organized meetups

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about Meetups, the answer should cover:

  • What they are: in-person and virtual gatherings organized by NHB members and coaches
  • Formats: regional meetups, coach-led gatherings, conference meetups, retreats, virtual events
  • How to find upcoming ones: Meetups section on the NHB platform, Home dashboard, or forum discussions
  • How to organize one: create a new meetup entry inviting other NHB members
  • Why they matter: the in-person layer of the NHB community; proximity and connection beyond the platform

docs.title: MindAI
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about MindAI — what it is, how to use it, what it can do, what it is trained on, who has access, whether it can replace coaches Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
MindAI is an AI assistant built into the NHB platform, trained on NHB's own teaching content. It helps members find answers faster, navigate the library, understand concepts that have been taught on calls, and get pointed to the right resources, coaches, or programs inside NHB.

MindAI is a tool, not a substitute for the coaches or the community. It is useful for looking things up, finding past calls on a specific topic, summarizing NHB concepts, and answering general member questions about how the platform works.

docs.title: What MindAI can help with
docs.text:
MindAI is built to answer questions about:

  • NHB content — what was taught on a specific call, what a concept means, where to find more on a topic
  • Platform features — how Fast Feedback, Hot Seats, Live Calls, the Forum, and other features work
  • Coaches and programs — who each coach is, what they teach, what their coaching program covers, when their calls are
  • Pricing and plans — what each membership tier includes and how the plans differ
  • Navigation — where to find specific content, sessions, or resources on the platform

For most "how does this work" or "what did Alen say about X" type questions, MindAI can deliver an answer directly or point the member to the right place.

docs.title: What MindAI will not do
docs.text:
There are specific things MindAI is deliberately cautious about:

  • Predict member results. MindAI will not tell a member how much money they will make, how long a specific strategy will take to work, or promise any outcome. Results depend on the individual, the market, the offer, and many variables outside of anything NHB or MindAI can control.
  • Comment negatively on competitors. MindAI will not characterize other companies, platforms, coaches, or communities negatively, regardless of what may exist in training content as candid opinion.
  • Disclose specific member earnings or private business data. Member financial information, even if it has been mentioned in community discussions, is not surfaced through MindAI.
  • Replace a coach's direct feedback. MindAI can explain NHB concepts and point members to relevant content, but it cannot look at a member's specific offer or copy and give expert feedback. That is what coaches do via Fast Feedback and Hot Seats.
  • Give legal, medical, financial, or tax advice. MindAI can talk about business and marketing topics NHB teaches, but it is not a substitute for licensed professional advice in regulated areas.

docs.title: How MindAI works
docs.text:
MindAI is powered by a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system. When a member asks a question, MindAI retrieves the most relevant content from a knowledge base of NHB materials and uses that content to generate an answer. The knowledge base includes official NHB documents (policies, feature docs, coach bios, program descriptions) and selected training content that has been prepared for retrieval.

MindAI is trained to prefer official NHB knowledge base documents over raw call transcripts when both are available, so member-facing answers reflect NHB's current positions on pricing, plans, coaches, programs, and policies rather than out-of-date statements from older calls.

Chat history is retained so members can return to a conversation and continue where they left off.

docs.title: Who has access
docs.text: MindAI is available to paying NHB members as part of the platform. Specific access may vary by tier — members should check their plan to see what is included, and upgrade if they want fuller access.

docs.title: Usage limits
docs.text: MindAI usage may have per-plan monthly limits. These limits are in place to keep the system performing reliably for all members. Members who hit a limit will see an in-app message.

docs.title: Where to find MindAI
docs.text: MindAI is accessible directly from the NHB platform's main navigation bar. Members can open it from anywhere in the app without leaving their current page.

docs.title: When to use MindAI vs when to ask a coach
docs.text:
Use MindAI when:

  • Looking up what was taught on a specific topic
  • Finding a past call, a resource, or a section of the library
  • Asking about how a platform feature works
  • Getting a quick refresher on an NHB concept
  • Figuring out which coach or program is most relevant to a specific question

Ask a coach (via Fast Feedback or Hot Seats) when:

  • The member wants feedback on their specific offer, copy, funnel, or work
  • The question requires a coach to look at the member's actual business
  • The member wants personalized strategy, not just information
  • The issue is nuanced enough that a human-to-human conversation is the right format

MindAI is meant to complement the coaching team, not replace them. For personalized work-on-your-business help, the path is always to a coach.

docs.title: Related features
docs.text:
• Library — the content archive MindAI pulls from
  • Fast Feedback — where to get personalized coach feedback on a member's own work
  • Hot Seats — where to get a live, real-time business review from a coach
  • Search — for when a member wants to browse results themselves rather than get an AI-generated answer

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about MindAI, the answer should cover:

  • What it is: an AI assistant trained on NHB content, built into the NHB platform
  • What it does well: finding information, answering platform and content questions, navigating the library, summarizing NHB concepts
  • What it doesn't do: predict results, replace coaches, comment on competitors, disclose private member info
  • How to access it: through the NHB platform navigation
  • When to use it versus asking a coach: MindAI for information and orientation, coaches for personalized feedback on real work

If a member asks MindAI to do something outside of its designed scope — predict their income, evaluate a competitor, review their specific offer in detail — MindAI should politely explain what it can and cannot do, and point the member toward the right resource (a coach, the relevant feature, or the appropriate NHB document) instead.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about notifications, alerts, email notifications, managing notification settings Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Notifications keep members aware of activity on the NHB platform that is relevant to them — replies to their forum threads, mentions, Fast Feedback responses from coaches, comments on their posts, coaching updates, and platform announcements.

docs.title: What members get notified about
docs.text:
The NHB notification system covers a range of events, including:

  • Fast Feedback reply — when an assigned coach submits a response to a member's Fast Feedback submission
  • Forum activity — replies to threads the member started, replies to comments, and mentions (@username)
  • Forum follows — new threads in followed categories or from followed members
  • Hot Seats — confirmation when a Hot Seat submission is accepted and upcoming
  • Live Calls — reminders for upcoming calls the member is attending
  • Coaching updates — messages from coaches and program-related announcements
  • Meetups — updates on Meetups the member has RSVP'd to
  • Owned Post notifications — when a member's hot seat submission is featured
  • Platform announcements — official NHB announcements about the platform, new features, or member updates

docs.title: How notifications are delivered
docs.text:
Notifications arrive through multiple channels:

  • In-app notifications — a notification center inside the NHB platform showing unread notifications with a count indicator
  • Email — certain key notifications (like Fast Feedback replies) are sent via email in addition to in-app, using the support@nhbnotify.com sender address and "Nothing Held Back" as the from name
  • Discord — mentions and activity in the NHB Discord server come through Discord's own notification system

docs.title: Managing notifications
docs.text:
Members can configure which notifications they receive and how through the NHB platform's settings. Common controls include:

  • Email notifications on/off for specific event types
  • Follow/unfollow specific forum categories or members
  • Mute specific threads or categories

Members who hit "Mark all as read" can clear their unread notification indicator across the entire system at once. This is particularly useful inside Fast Feedback, where a dedicated "Mark all as read" button handles clearing unread submissions.

docs.title: Where to find Notifications
docs.text:
• Notification icon — typically top-right of the NHB platform, with an unread count badge
  • Settings — to configure notification preferences

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about Notifications, the answer should cover:

  • What they are: alerts about activity inside NHB that is relevant to the member
  • Types of events: Fast Feedback replies, forum activity, mentions, Hot Seat confirmations, call reminders, coaching updates, announcements
  • How they are delivered: in-app notifications, email for key events, Discord for chat activity
  • How to manage: platform settings allow members to configure which notifications they receive and how
  • Where to find: the notification icon in the top navigation of the platform

docs.title: Partner Program
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about the NHB Partner Program, becoming a partner, affiliate, referral commission, partner dashboard, payouts Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The NHB Partner Program is the affiliate and referral program for members and outside partners who want to refer people to NHB and earn commission on successful referrals. Partners share a unique referral link, track referrals through an external partner dashboard, and receive payouts on referred members who join NHB Pro or Fast Forward.

The program is open to qualified members and partners. Members can apply through the Partner Program page on the NHB platform.

docs.title: How the program works
docs.text:
The high-level flow:

  1. A member or qualified partner applies to the Partner Program
  2. Once approved, the partner receives a unique referral link and access to a partner dashboard
  3. The partner shares their link — typically in content, emails, social posts, or direct introductions
  4. When someone signs up to NHB through the partner's link, the referral is tracked
  5. The partner earns commission on the referred member's NHB subscription according to the program's current terms
  6. Payouts are processed on the program's defined schedule

docs.title: Referral tracking
docs.text:
Referral tracking runs on an external partner dashboard integrated with NHB. The external tracking system (currently Everflow) handles the technical work of attributing referrals to the correct partner. Partners log into the dashboard to see:

  • Referrals generated (clicks, sign-ups)
  • Earnings accrued
  • Payout history and upcoming payouts
  • Promotional assets (banners, copy examples)

The partner dashboard is accessed through a link on the NHB Partner Program page.

docs.title: What partners can earn
docs.text:
Commission rates, payout structure, and qualifying member types (Pro, Fast Forward, coaching programs) are defined by the current Partner Program terms. Members should refer to the Partner Program page on the NHB platform for the authoritative current rates, because these can change over time.

In general, partners earn a percentage commission on qualifying referred members' subscriptions. Commissions are typically recurring for as long as the referred member maintains their NHB subscription, subject to the program's current terms.

docs.title: Who can become a partner
docs.text:
The Partner Program is generally open to:

  • NHB members in good standing — especially members who have been active and successful enough in the community to authentically refer others
  • Operators and content creators in adjacent spaces — marketers, coaches, consultants, and content creators whose audiences would benefit from NHB
  • Existing NHB partners — who continue with the program as long as they remain in good standing

Approval is at NHB's discretion. The program is designed to attract partners who will represent NHB authentically and refer members who are a good fit, rather than pure affiliates running cold traffic to a landing page.

docs.title: How to apply
docs.text:
Members interested in the Partner Program can apply through the Partner Program page on the NHB platform. The application typically involves:

  1. Filling out the application form with information about the applicant, their audience, and how they plan to promote NHB
  2. NHB reviews and approves qualified applicants
  3. Approved partners gain access to their dashboard, referral link, and promotional materials

docs.title: What the Partner Program page includes
docs.text:
The /partner_program page on the NHB platform is the main landing and information page for the program. It typically includes:

  • Program intro — what the Partner Program is and why NHB runs it
  • Partner benefits — what partners get (commissions, dashboard access, promotional assets, community recognition)
  • Testimonials — existing partner stories and wins
  • How the program works — the numbered process of how referrals and commissions flow
  • Earnings and payout details — current commission structure and payout cadence
  • FAQ — common questions about the program
  • Dashboard access — button to the external partner dashboard for existing partners

Members should refer to the Partner Program page on the NHB platform for current specifics, since terms and rates can change.

docs.title: What partners can and can't do
docs.text:
Good partner practice:

  • Referring people who would genuinely benefit from NHB based on what they are building
  • Sharing authentic testimonials and results
  • Linking to NHB from content, emails, or direct introductions where it fits contextually
  • Using the promotional materials NHB provides (banners, copy) or creating their own with NHB's approval

Not acceptable:

  • Making income claims on NHB's behalf that violate NHB's income and results policy
  • Misrepresenting what NHB is, how it works, or what it costs
  • Running cold paid traffic to NHB without approval from NHB
  • Using misleading, clickbait, or spammy promotion tactics
  • Criticizing NHB competitors in a way that violates NHB's competitor policy
  • Sharing NHB members' private information or behind-the-scenes content

Partners who violate these standards can have their partner access revoked without commission payout on any referrals generated through prohibited methods.

docs.title: Relationship to NHB's older affiliate system
docs.text: NHB previously ran parts of its affiliate tracking internally inside the Bubble platform. That internal system has been deprecated and the full affiliate tracking now runs through the external partner dashboard (Everflow). Members who were active in the older system should use the current partner dashboard going forward.

docs.title: Where to find the Partner Program
docs.text:
• Main platform page — /partner_program on the NHB platform
  • NHB navigation — look for Partner Program, Affiliate, or Partner links in the platform navigation
  • Partner dashboard — accessed through the link on the Partner Program page (external site)

docs.title: Related documents
docs.text:
• Plans and pricing — for understanding what tiers partners can earn commission on
  • Competitor policy — partners should respect the competitor policy in their promotion
  • Income and results policy — partners should respect the income policy when marketing NHB to their audiences

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about the Partner Program, the answer should cover:

  • What it is: NHB's affiliate and referral program where partners earn commission on successful referrals
  • How to apply: through the Partner Program page on the NHB platform
  • Who qualifies: NHB members in good standing, and operators or content creators whose audiences would benefit from NHB; approval is at NHB's discretion
  • How tracking works: external partner dashboard (Everflow) tracks clicks, sign-ups, earnings, and payouts
  • How payouts work: commission on qualifying referrals according to the current program terms; for specifics, refer to the Partner Program page
  • What partners can and can't do: authentic promotion is encouraged; misleading claims, income claims, or competitor criticism violate NHB policies and can revoke access

For specific questions about commission rates, payout schedules, or application status, members should contact NHB support or check the Partner Program page for current terms.

docs.title: Playlists
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about playlists, curated learning paths, learning sequences Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Playlists are curated sequences of content inside NHB — ordered lists of Live Calls, Library entries, course lessons, and resources organized around a specific learning path or topic. Where the Library is the searchable archive, Playlists give members a starting point when they don't know where to begin on a new topic.

docs.title: How Playlists work
docs.text:
A Playlist is a structured sequence where one piece of content leads into the next. Examples of playlists a member might find:

  • A sequence of Alen's calls on offer construction, ordered from fundamentals through advanced
  • A Meta Ads learning path that walks through Loren's core frameworks in the intended order
  • A copywriting playlist that progresses from Chris's P.I.G. Method basics through mastery application
  • A CRO learning path from Brandon that sequences his Library of Truth Trainings

Members work through a Playlist in order and can pick it back up where they left off. Progress tracking helps members see what they have completed and what's next.

docs.title: Who builds Playlists
docs.text: Playlists are typically curated by NHB or by individual coaches to guide members through a specific body of work in a sensible order. Members can also bookmark playlists to return to them later.

docs.title: Where to find Playlists
docs.text:
• Main platform navigation — Playlists section on the NHB platform
  • Library — Playlists appear alongside individual Library items, grouped as sequences
  • Coaching program pages — some coaches publish curated playlists specifically for their program members

docs.title: Related features
docs.text:
• Library — Playlists pull from Library content; members can browse the Library directly if they prefer
  • Courses — courses are more formally structured learning programs; playlists are lighter-weight curated sequences
  • Bookmarks — members can bookmark a playlist to come back to it

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about Playlists, the answer should cover:

  • What they are: curated, ordered sequences of NHB content around a specific topic or learning path
  • How they differ from courses: lighter-weight, drawn from existing Library content, not a full course curriculum
  • How they differ from the Library: they impose an intended order, whereas the Library is browsable/searchable
  • Where to find them: Playlists section of the NHB platform, or surfaced inside the Library

docs.title: Public Profile
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about member profiles, public profile pages, follow system, bio, links, stats Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Every NHB member has a Public Profile — a page inside the platform where other members can see who they are, what they do, what they are working on, and connect with them. Profiles turn NHB from a list of usernames into a real community of identified operators, where members can find each other by industry, niche, coaching program, and other attributes.

docs.title: What a profile includes
docs.text:
A member's Public Profile can display:

  • Basic identity — name, profile photo, location, and a short bio
  • Industry and niche — the member's market, sector, and what they build
  • Work — current projects, businesses, and roles the member wants to highlight
  • Links — social profiles, websites, and other relevant URLs
  • Coaching programs — which NHB coaching programs the member is enrolled in
  • Followers and following — lists of members the user follows and is followed by
  • Activity feed — a stream of the member's public activity on the platform (forum posts, wins, Fast Feedback submissions, and more)
  • Stats — likes, bookmarks, and other engagement markers where relevant

Members can customize what appears on their profile through their settings.

docs.title: Following
docs.text:
Members can follow other members. Following adds the followed member's activity to the follower's feed and enables notifications on new activity. Unfollowing reverses this. The follow system is a direct database operation, not a workflow, so it is fast and immediate.

The Rolodex feature inside the Connect section of NHB provides a searchable directory of members, including their profile information, which is how many members discover and follow each other.

docs.title: Privacy and access
docs.text:
Member profiles are visible to other logged-in NHB members. Free members and guests typically have limited or no access to browse member profiles, depending on the specific information.

Members can control which information appears on their profile. Some fields are platform-internal only (not publicly displayed), while others (name, bio, links, coaching programs, work) are intended for member-to-member visibility.

docs.title: Where to find Profiles
docs.text:
• Member's own profile — through the account menu on the NHB platform
  • Other members' profiles — click a member's name or avatar anywhere on the platform (forum posts, comments, member lists)
  • Rolodex — searchable member directory inside the Connect section

docs.title: Related features
docs.text:
• Rolodex — the member directory and search tool for finding other members
  • Forum — where members often discover each other before navigating to profiles
  • Notifications — get notified when new followers connect
  • Bookmarks — follow members alongside bookmarking content

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about Public Profiles, the answer should cover:

  • What they are: a page per member displaying identity, work, niche, links, coaching programs, followers, and public activity
  • How to view: click a member's name or avatar, or find them via the Rolodex
  • How to customize: through the member's account settings
  • Follow system: members can follow each other to see activity and get notifications on new posts
  • Privacy: generally visible to other logged-in members; members can control what appears on their profile

docs.title: Resources
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about NHB Resources, templates, swipe files, tools, downloadable assets, external reference links Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Resources inside NHB are practical assets members use to execute work faster — templates, swipe files, reference guides, tools, and curated external references. Where courses teach the thinking and live calls teach the strategy, Resources are what members reach for when they need to ship something now.

docs.title: What counts as a Resource
docs.text:
The NHB Resources section includes:

  • Templates — offer frameworks, funnel structures, email templates, copy templates, ad templates, sales letter outlines
  • Swipe files — Alen's personal swipe stash of ads, emails, sales letters, VSLs, and landing pages, plus material contributed by the community
  • Tools — links and references to tools members use across marketing, ads, email, CRO, and AI
  • External references — curated books, courses, and guides worth knowing about outside of NHB
  • Resource documents — downloadable PDFs, Google Docs, and other supporting assets

Each resource typically has a clear description of what it is, who it's for, and how to apply it in a member's own business.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
Resources are plan-gated, similar to other content inside NHB. Most Resources are available at the NHB Pro level, with some additional resources specifically available to Fast Forward members and Coaching Program members.

Coaching program members get access to their coach's specific resource library — for example, Brandon's CRO templates and split-test playbooks are inside the CRO Accelerator member vault.

docs.title: How members use Resources
docs.text:
The typical use pattern:

  1. A member is building something — an offer, a funnel, a sequence, an ad — and needs a starting point
  2. They open the Resources section and browse or search for the relevant template or swipe file
  3. They download or copy the asset and adapt it to their own business
  4. They can optionally get coach feedback on the adaptation via Fast Feedback or Hot Seats

This cuts the execution time for most marketing work dramatically because members are not rebuilding from scratch what has already been proven to work.

docs.title: Filtering and search
docs.text:
Members can browse Resources by:

  • Type — templates vs swipe files vs tools vs external references
  • Topic — marketing discipline (ads, copy, email, CRO, offers, and so on)
  • Coach — resources from a specific coach's program
  • Plan tier — only resources the member has access to are shown

Full-text search across Resource titles and descriptions is supported through the platform's search.

docs.title: Where to find Resources
docs.text:
• Main platform navigation — Resources is a top-level section on the NHB platform
  • Coaching program pages — coach-specific resources live inside each program's page
  • Library — Resources often appear alongside related content in the Library

docs.title: Related features
docs.text:
• Library — Resources and Library content are interlinked; Resources often appear inside courses and live calls
  • Courses — many course lessons include Resources as accompanying assets
  • Swipe files — a subset of Resources specifically focused on ad creative, email, and sales copy examples

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about Resources, the answer should cover:

  • What they are: practical assets members use to execute faster — templates, swipe files, tools, and references
  • What's included: Alen's swipe stash, coach-specific templates, tools, and curated external references
  • How to access: Resources section on the NHB platform, with plan and coaching program gating
  • How to use them: browse or search, download, adapt to member's business
  • Coach-specific resource libraries: inside each coaching program for members of that program

Any questions about specific revenue results from using a template or swipe file should follow the NHB income and results policy.

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB platform feature document Applies to: Any question about searching inside NHB, finding content, the search bar, what is searchable Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Search inside NHB is a full-text search across content the member has access to — Library entries, forum threads, Resources, Fast Feedback submissions, and more. The search is powered by Algolia, which provides fast, fuzzy, typo-tolerant searching across large amounts of content.

docs.title: What is searchable
docs.text:
Members can search across:

  • Library content — live call recordings, Hot Seats, courses, insights, and other archive content
  • Forum threads — titles, bodies, and comments in categories the member has access to
  • Resources — templates, swipe files, and other Resource items
  • Fast Feedback submissions — public Fast Feedback posts and responses
  • Coaches and coaching programs — finding a specific coach's page or program

The search typically returns results grouped by content type, so members can see matching live calls, matching forum threads, and matching resources as separate result clusters.

docs.title: How to search
docs.text:
Members can search in two main ways:

  • Main platform search bar — usually found in the top navigation, accessible from anywhere on the platform
  • Feature-specific search — individual features like Fast Feedback, the Library, and the Forum have their own in-context search

Members can search by topic, keyword, coach name, concept, or any other free-text query. The search is typo-tolerant and handles partial matches.

docs.title: Plan-gated results
docs.text: Search only returns content the member has access to based on their plan and coaching program enrollment. Content gated to Fast Forward does not appear in Pro members' search results, and coaching-program-specific content only appears for members of that program.

docs.title: Search and MindAI
docs.text:
For members who prefer to ask a question rather than browse search results, MindAI can often answer questions about NHB content without requiring the member to search and read results manually. The two features complement each other:

  • Search — best when the member wants to browse results themselves and pick the right piece of content
  • MindAI — best when the member wants a direct answer synthesized from NHB content

docs.title: Where to find Search
docs.text:
• Main navigation — the search bar typically lives in the top bar of the NHB platform, accessible on every page
  • Within features — Library, Forum, and Fast Feedback all have their own in-context search

docs.title: Related features
docs.text:
• Library — uses the platform's search internally
  • Forum — uses the platform's search internally
  • MindAI — AI-powered alternative to searching manually
  • Bookmarks — an alternative to search when members already know what they want and have saved it

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about Search, the answer should cover:

  • What it is: full-text search across NHB content the member has access to
  • What's searchable: Library entries, forum threads, Resources, Fast Feedback submissions, coaching programs
  • How it works: powered by Algolia, fast, typo-tolerant, and fuzzy-matching
  • Where to find the search bar: top navigation of the platform, plus feature-specific search within Library, Forum, and Fast Feedback
  • Plan gating: search results only include content the member has access to
  • When to use MindAI instead: when a direct answer is faster than browsing search results

docs.title: NHB Policy on Competitors and Comparison Questions
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB policy document Applies to: MindAI responses, member-facing statements, any AI-retrieved answer involving a company, platform, community, or person outside of NHB Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Nothing Held Back does not speak negatively about other companies, platforms, communities, coaches, tools, or industry figures. This policy applies to every answer retrieved and surfaced to NHB members, regardless of what source material may exist in training content, call transcripts, internal discussions, or member conversations.

docs.title: Policy
docs.text:
NHB operates on a zero-negative standard when discussing any entity outside the NHB community. This standard applies to:

  • Other online communities, masterminds, membership programs, or coaching groups
  • Software platforms, funnel builders, course platforms, CRM tools, email tools, ad platforms, or analytics products
  • Marketing agencies, service providers, or freelancers outside NHB
  • Public industry figures, educators, gurus, authors, or influencers
  • Specific companies, brands, or business models
  • Products competing with anything a member might build or sell

On any of these topics, NHB communications remain neutral, respectful, and focused on what NHB offers rather than on evaluating or criticizing what others offer. No direct comparison, no ranking, no "better than" or "worse than" language, no characterization of quality, pricing, results, or approach of any outside party.

docs.title: Why this policy exists
docs.text:
NHB's training content is candid. Calls, hot seats, and member discussions often include frank opinions about specific companies, platforms, and industry figures. Those opinions are personal perspectives shared in context, not official NHB positions. They are not meant to be retrieved as standalone statements or repeated to members in AI-generated answers.

Repeating those opinions as if they were NHB's stance creates three problems. It misrepresents NHB as an organization that publicly criticizes competitors, which NHB is not. It exposes NHB to reputational and legal risk around statements NHB did not authorize. And it gives members a lower-quality answer than the frame NHB actually wants them to have, which is focused on building their own business, not on evaluating others.

docs.title: How to handle common question types
Direct questions about a named competitor
docs.text:
When a member asks about a specific outside company, platform, or person by name, the answer should acknowledge the question, decline to characterize the named party, and redirect to what NHB provides and how NHB approaches the underlying need.

Sanctioned response frame:

NHB focuses on its own approach rather than evaluating other platforms or communities. What NHB offers in this area is [brief, accurate description of the relevant NHB capability]. If a member shares what they are trying to accomplish, NHB can point them to the specific resources, trainings, or coaches inside the platform that are most relevant.

docs.title: Comparison questions
docs.text:
When a member asks "How does NHB compare to [X]?" or "Is [X] better than NHB?" or "Why should someone choose NHB over [X]?":

  • The answer should not characterize the competitor's quality, pricing, results, approach, coaches, or community.
  • The answer should not make any claim about whether one option is better than the other.
  • The answer should describe what NHB offers, what makes NHB's approach distinct, and invite the member to evaluate fit based on their own goals.

Sanctioned response frame:

NHB is a transformational environment for entrepreneurs. It combines direct coaching from operators who are actively running offers, a library of strategies and frameworks, Fast Feedback on member work, Hot Seats for live problem-solving, and a community that spans six-, seven-, eight-, and nine-figure operators across many industries. The focus is on teaching members how to think about marketing, offers, and scaling, not just handing out templates. Every member's goals and situation are different, so the best way to evaluate fit is to look at what NHB actually provides and whether that matches what a member is trying to build.

docs.title: Questions that include criticism of a competitor in the retrieved source
docs.text: If a retrieval surfaces a transcript passage, hot seat recording, or member comment that criticizes a named company or person, that content must not be quoted, paraphrased, or summarized in the answer to the member. Answers on these topics should be generated from this policy document instead, regardless of what other retrieved content might suggest.

docs.title: Questions asking for opinions on industry trends, tools, or practices
docs.text: Neutral framing is always preferred. Describe approaches in terms of tradeoffs and use cases rather than ranking. Describe tools by what they do rather than whether they are good or bad. When a member asks "Is [tool X] any good?" or "Should someone use [platform Y]?", the answer should describe what the tool is designed for and what NHB teaches about the underlying skill or outcome, without evaluating the tool itself.

docs.title: What to say instead of comparing
docs.text:
When the conversation drifts toward comparison, NHB can always redirect to what NHB itself provides:

  • Approach: NHB teaches entrepreneurs how to think about marketing, offers, and scaling using the Socratic method, rather than handing out fill-in-the-blank systems or cookie-cutter formulas.
  • Coaches: NHB's coaches are operators actively working on offers in real markets, not career educators teaching outdated tactics. They bring current strategy and real-world perspective into every training and hot seat.
  • Access: Members get direct coaching through weekly trainings, Fast Feedback on their own work, Hot Seats for live problem-solving, and a community that supports them at every stage of their business.
  • Breadth: The NHB platform covers offers, funnels, copywriting, paid ads, email, CRO, scaling, launches, lead generation, brand, and more, taught as an integrated system rather than isolated tactics.
  • Community: The member base spans every stage of the entrepreneurial journey, from new builders through nine-figure operators across many industries, which creates the kind of proximity and environment that most communities cannot offer.

These are factual descriptions of NHB, not comparisons. They can be used to answer "why NHB" questions without ever evaluating a competitor.

docs.title: Scope of the policy
docs.text:
This policy applies to:

  • Every AI-generated answer surfaced to any NHB member through MindAI
  • Any retrieved content that references an outside company, platform, or person
  • Any question that could be interpreted as asking for a comparison, opinion, or evaluation of an outside party
  • Any topic where retrieved training content contains candid opinions about the outside party

When in doubt, the default is to not comment on anyone or anything outside NHB, and to redirect the answer to what NHB provides and how NHB can help the member move forward.

docs.title: Examples of what must not appear in answers
docs.text:
The following types of statements must not be surfaced to members, regardless of whether they appear in training content:

  • Statements that a specific outside platform or company is overpriced, underpriced, low-quality, high-quality, behind the curve, or ahead of the curve
  • Statements evaluating the results, conversion rates, or performance of a specific outside company or offer
  • Statements comparing the coaches, trainers, or personalities associated with an outside community to NHB's coaches or community
  • Statements that a specific outside tool is broken, outdated, poorly built, or inferior to an alternative
  • Statements that a specific public figure teaches bad advice, is out of touch, or is not credible
  • Any direct quote or close paraphrase from training content that targets a named outside party

If a retrieval contains content of this type, the answer should be generated from this policy document and should redirect to what NHB offers.

docs.title: NHB Policy on Income Claims and Results
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB policy document Applies to: MindAI responses, member-facing statements, any AI-retrieved answer involving earnings, revenue, business outcomes, or results Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Nothing Held Back does not make specific income claims, guaranteed-results claims, or predictions about what any member will earn, achieve, or build. This policy applies to every answer retrieved and surfaced to NHB members, regardless of what source material may exist in training content, call transcripts, member wins, or internal discussions.

NHB's training content includes candid discussion of real numbers, real wins, and real results. Those are personal accounts shared in context, not forecasts, promises, or sanctioned case studies. They must not be surfaced as predictions, typical outcomes, or expected results for any member.

docs.title: Policy
docs.text:
NHB communications will not:

  • Predict that any specific member will earn a specific amount of money
  • State that any specific strategy, offer, or approach will produce a specific revenue outcome
  • Guarantee results of any kind from membership, coaching, or applying taught material
  • Characterize what members "typically" earn or "should" earn
  • Cite specific member earnings, revenue figures, or business outcomes as representative examples
  • Name specific members by name in connection with specific income figures in AI-generated answers, unless the member has explicitly and publicly authorized that disclosure
  • Repeat specific revenue numbers surfaced from training transcripts as if those numbers represent promised or typical outcomes
  • Use historical results to imply future results

docs.title: Why this policy exists
docs.text:
Specific income claims and guaranteed-outcome language create three problems. They mislead members about what NHB actually offers, which is education, environment, and support, not a predictable financial outcome. They expose NHB to regulatory and legal risk under advertising and earnings-claim guidelines in multiple jurisdictions. And they do a disservice to the members themselves by setting expectations that ignore the reality that results depend entirely on the individual member's effort, skill, market, timing, existing assets, and many other variables outside NHB's control.

NHB's training content is candid. Coaches and members discuss real numbers, real wins, and real losses openly. That openness is part of the culture and is valuable inside the community. But those specific numbers, wins, and losses are personal accounts shared in context. They are not marketing claims, promises, or representations about what any other member will experience.

docs.title: How to handle common question types
"How much can I make with NHB?"
docs.text:
This question must be answered without any specific income figure.

Sanctioned response frame:

NHB does not make predictions about what any member will earn. Member results depend on many factors, including the member's existing skills, market, offer, effort level, execution speed, and many variables outside of what NHB controls. What NHB provides is the training, coaching, feedback, tools, community, and environment designed to help members develop stronger skills and make better decisions. What a member does with that is up to them.

docs.title: "How much did [specific member] make?"
docs.text:
This question must be redirected. NHB does not disclose member financial information in AI-generated answers, even if the member has mentioned a figure in a training call or community discussion.

Sanctioned response frame:

NHB does not disclose specific member earnings or business details through MindAI. If a member has publicly shared their own results and wants to share them again, they can do so directly in the community. For general questions about what members are working on or the kinds of projects being built, MindAI can describe the breadth of the community without tying specific numbers to specific people.

docs.title: "Is it worth joining? Will I make back the money?"
docs.text:
This must be answered without any return-on-investment prediction.

Sanctioned response frame:

That depends entirely on what a member brings to the experience and what they do with it. NHB provides training, coaching, Fast Feedback, Hot Seats, and a community designed to help entrepreneurs develop the skills and judgment to build better businesses. Some members apply it intensely and see fast progress. Others take longer. Some do not apply it and see nothing. NHB cannot predict what any individual member will do. The best way to evaluate fit is to look at what NHB actually provides and whether the training, community, and environment match what the member is trying to build.

docs.title: "What results should I expect in [timeframe]?"
docs.text:
This must be answered without any specific outcome forecast.

Sanctioned response frame:

NHB does not project timelines or results for individual members. Building a business is nonlinear and depends on many factors specific to the member, the market, and the offer. What NHB provides is the training, coaching, and environment to help members make faster and better decisions over time. The pace of a member's progress depends on the member's starting point, the work they put in, and many variables outside NHB's control.

docs.title: Questions about member "success stories" or "case studies"
docs.text:
General, non-numeric descriptions of the kinds of things members are working on are fine. Specific revenue figures, earnings claims, or member-by-name financial details are not.

Sanctioned response frame:

The NHB community includes entrepreneurs at many stages, from new builders through operators running established businesses across many industries. Members work on offers in health, finance, coaching, e-commerce, software, supplements, education, and many other markets. For current case studies or wins a member wants to highlight, the Wall of Wins and community posts are the right place to explore, since those are firsthand accounts members have chosen to share themselves.

docs.title: What to say instead of income claims
docs.text:
When a member asks about what is possible or what they could achieve, the answer should focus on:

  • What NHB teaches: How to think about marketing, offers, copywriting, ads, CRO, scaling, and launches. The skills and judgment members develop, not the numbers they will produce.
  • What NHB provides: Direct coaching from operators actively building offers, Fast Feedback on member work, Hot Seats for live problem-solving, a community for support and proximity, and a library of trainings and resources across every topic in modern marketing.
  • The kind of transformation NHB is built to create: Better thinking. Better decisions. Better execution. Better positioning. Better offers. The member becomes more capable over time. What they do with that capability is up to them.
  • How members can evaluate fit: By looking at what NHB provides, who the coaches are, what gets taught, and whether the approach and environment match what the member is trying to build.

None of these require making a specific numeric claim.

docs.title: Scope of the policy
docs.text:
This policy applies to:

  • Every AI-generated answer surfaced to any NHB member through MindAI
  • Any retrieved content that contains specific revenue figures, earnings claims, or outcome predictions
  • Any question that could be interpreted as asking for a forecast, guarantee, or typical-outcome estimate
  • Any topic where retrieved training content contains candid discussion of numbers or results

When in doubt, the default is to describe what NHB provides and what members learn, without attaching any specific number, timeline, or outcome prediction to the answer.

docs.title: Examples of what must not appear in answers
docs.text:
The following types of statements must not be surfaced to members, regardless of whether they appear in training content:

  • "Members typically earn [figure]"
  • "After joining, you should expect [figure] in [timeframe]"
  • "[Member name] made [figure] after applying this"
  • "With this strategy you can make [figure]"
  • "This offer typically converts at [rate] and produces [figure]"
  • "If you follow this approach, your revenue will [specific prediction]"
  • Any direct quote or close paraphrase from training content that attaches a specific revenue figure to a specific member by name
  • Any statement that characterizes what a "typical" member outcome looks like in dollar terms

If a retrieval contains content of this type, the answer should be generated from this policy document and should describe what NHB provides in terms of skills, coaching, and environment, not in terms of numeric outcomes.

docs.title: NHB Refund and Cancellation Policy
docs.text: Document type: Official NHB policy document Applies to: Any question about refunds, cancellations, billing cycle, End of Cycle processing, pausing, what happens to member access after cancelling Last updated: April 2026

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
NHB operates on a straightforward refund and cancellation policy: all sales are final, no refunds are offered, and members can cancel month-to-month at any time. Cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing cycle, with members retaining full access until that point.

This policy applies equally to NHB Pro, Fast Forward, and every coaching program add-on.

docs.title: Refund policy
docs.text:
NHB does not offer refunds on memberships or coaching programs. If a program or plan is not working for a member, the correct action is to cancel before the next billing cycle. Refunds are not granted, even for partial months, inactive periods, or unused coaching sessions.

This policy exists for a specific reason: coaching programs require the coach's time and attention from day one. Group calls, Fast Feedback, Hot Seats, and community access are live services being delivered. Once a member is inside a program, the cost of providing that service has already been incurred whether or not the member shows up. Refunds therefore are not part of the model.

docs.title: Cancellation — how it works
docs.text:
Any member can cancel their NHB membership or any coaching program add-on at any time. There are no long-term contracts. Cancellation is month-to-month.

Cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing cycle. The member retains full access to everything they paid for until that cycle ends. Only at the end of the billing cycle does access reduce to a lower tier (or no access, if cancelling entirely).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: A member paid for NHB Pro on the 15th of the month. On the 28th, they decide to cancel. Their cancellation is processed, but access continues until the 14th of the following month (the end of the original billing cycle they paid for). On the 15th, access steps down.

docs.title: Cancellation cascade for coaching programs
docs.text:
Because coaching programs are add-ons to an active NHB Pro or Fast Forward membership, there is an automatic cascade:

  • If a member cancels their NHB Pro or Fast Forward base membership, all their coaching program add-ons automatically cancel too at the same billing cycle boundary.
  • If a member downgrades to Free, they lose access to all coaching programs.
  • If a member cancels only one coaching program but keeps their base membership, the other programs and base membership remain active.

docs.title: Downgrade (Pro → Free, FF → Pro) timing
docs.text:
Downgrades follow the same End of Cycle rule. A downgrade scheduled mid-cycle does not take effect until the current billing period ends. The member keeps their higher-tier access until the downgrade date.

Upgrades are the opposite: they take effect immediately. A Free member upgrading to Pro gets Pro access instantly at checkout.

docs.title: Pausing a membership
docs.text:
Fast Forward offers a Pause Plan for members who need to temporarily pause their FF membership. Specific terms are provided at the point of pausing — for example, the pause may cover a defined time window during which the member maintains community access but does not attend live Alen calls, with billing adjusted accordingly.

NHB Pro and coaching programs do not currently have a formal pause option. The standard path for a member who needs a break is to cancel before the next billing cycle, then rejoin when ready.

docs.title: What happens to access after cancellation
docs.text:
When a member cancels and their final billing cycle ends:

  • Library, live calls, resources, courses — access ends. Content is no longer available to the member.
  • Forum and Discord — access ends. The member can no longer post or view member-only discussion.
  • Fast Feedback and Hot Seats — no more submissions or attendance.
  • Coaching programs — no more access to program-specific calls, community, or coach library.
  • Previously submitted content (forum posts, Fast Feedback submissions) — typically remains on the platform for other members to reference but the canceled member loses access to log in and see it.
  • Profile — typically remains on the platform but without active access.

Members who rejoin later regain access to the platform based on their new plan. Prior activity history may or may not be preserved depending on the rejoin path.

docs.title: Charge disputes and chargebacks
docs.text: Members who have a concern about a specific charge should contact NHB support first rather than filing a chargeback with their card issuer. Chargebacks can result in account restrictions and complicate the relationship. NHB support will address legitimate billing concerns directly.

docs.title: Payment failures
docs.text:
If a recurring payment fails, InfusionSoft retries the charge up to 5 times according to its standard schedule. If all retries fail, the subscription is canceled by both InfusionSoft and NHB. There is no mid-retry recovery pathway — once the subscription is canceled due to payment failure, the member must re-subscribe from scratch to regain access.

Members who want to prevent payment failure can update their payment method in advance through their account settings or at the ThriveCart payment update page (grow.thrivecart.com/updateinfo/).

docs.title: How to cancel
docs.text:
Members can cancel through:

  • NHB platform account settings — the primary path for most members
  • ThriveCart — for members whose billing is on ThriveCart
  • NHB support — if a member has difficulty cancelling through the platform, support can handle it directly

docs.title: Summary for answering member questions
docs.text:
When a member asks about refunds or cancellations, the answer should cover:

  • Refunds: None. All sales are final. Cancel before the next cycle if a plan is not working.
  • How to cancel: Through account settings, ThriveCart, or NHB support. Month-to-month, no contracts.
  • When cancellation takes effect: End of the current billing cycle. Access continues until that date.
  • Downgrade timing: Downgrades are End of Cycle. Upgrades are immediate.
  • Coaching program cascade: Cancelling base Pro or FF membership automatically cancels all coaching program add-ons.
  • Pause option: Fast Forward has a Pause Plan. Pro and coaching programs do not.
  • What happens to access after cancelling: Library, live calls, forum, Discord, coaching programs all lose access at the cycle end.

Any questions about making an exception to the refund policy should be directed to NHB support rather than handled by MindAI. The policy is not discretionary, but a member with a legitimate billing concern should be able to reach a human on the NHB team.

docs.title: Table of Contents
docs.text:
1. Purpose & Scope

docs.title: 1. Purpose & Scope
docs.text:
This SOP defines how the Alpha Four team uses Claude for AI-assisted development alongside GitHub for version control. It establishes standards to prevent merge conflicts, ensure code consistency, and integrate AI-generated code safely into shared repositories.

Who this covers: All engineers working on any Alpha Four repository who use Claude (via Claude.ai or the API) to generate, edit, or review code.

docs.title: 2. Guiding Principles
docs.text:
• Claude is a collaborator, not an authority. Always review AI-generated code before committing.
  • Small, focused changes. Each Claude session should target one concern — a function, a module, a bug fix.
  • Context is king. Claude has no memory between sessions; always re-supply relevant context.
  • Transparency. Add a note in PR descriptions when significant portions were AI-assisted.
  • Humans own the repo. Claude never has direct push access; all changes flow through PR review.

docs.title: 3. Branch Strategy
docs.text:
Use the following branching conventions for all repositories:

Branch Purpose Who creates it main Production-ready code only CI/CD pipeline develop Integration branch for completed features Repo maintainer feature/<ticket-id>-<slug> New feature work Any engineer fix/<ticket-id>-<slug> Bug fixes Any engineer claude/<ticket-id>-<desc> Exploratory AI-generated code Any engineer

✅ Good branch name: feature/REC-42-watch-next-cosine or claude/REC-42-embedding-schema-draft

❌ Avoid: claude-stuff or natalie-test-branch or wip

docs.title: 4.1 Before You Start a Session
docs.text:
1. Pull the latest changes from your base branch before opening a Claude session.
  2. Create or switch to your working branch: git checkout -b feature/<ticket-id>-<slug>
  3. Paste the relevant context into Claude at the start of the session (see Section 5).
  4. State your goal clearly in the first message — avoid vague openers like "help me with my project".

docs.title: 4.2 During the Session
docs.text:
• Work file-by-file. Do not ask Claude to rewrite multiple unrelated files in one prompt.
  • After each significant generation, copy the output into your editor and run it locally before continuing.
  • If Claude produces a large diff, break it into smaller commits by concern (schema change, service layer, tests).
  • Flag uncertainty: if Claude hedges or says "you may need to adjust," treat that as a required manual review step.

docs.title: 4.3 After the Session
docs.text:
1. Run your full test suite before staging any files.
  2. Do a git diff review of everything Claude touched — line by line.
  3. Remove any debug code, placeholder comments, or hallucinated imports before committing.
  4. Write a clear commit message (see Section 6).

docs.title: 5. Context Template for Claude Sessions
docs.text:
Paste this block at the start of every new Claude session. Fill in the blanks; omit irrelevant sections.

## Session Context
Project: Alpha Four — RAG Recommendation Engine
Stack: [e.g. TypeScript · Supabase pgvector · Next.js]
Branch: feature/<ticket-id>-<slug>
Ticket: [link or ID]

## Relevant Files (paste key snippets or describe)
- Schema: documents table (content_id, content_type, content, embedding, metadata JSONB, created_at)
- [Paste other relevant schema / types / interfaces]

## Goal for this session
[One specific task — e.g. 'Write the cosine similarity query for Watch Next']

## Constraints / Conventions
[e.g. 'Use snake_case for DB columns', 'No default exports', 'Zod for validation']

docs.title: 6. Commit Message Convention
docs.text:
All commits — AI-assisted or not — follow Conventional Commits format:

<type>(<scope>): <short summary>  [max 72 chars]

[optional body — what and why, not how]

[optional footer: Refs #42  |  ai-assisted: yes]
Type When to use Example feat New feature or capability feat(recommendations): add cosine similarity query fix Bug fix fix(embeddings): handle null content_type in upsert refactor Code change with no behaviour change refactor(vector-store): extract similarity fn test Adding or updating tests test(watch-next): add pgvector distance edge cases chore Tooling, deps, config chore: upgrade supabase-js to 2.43 docs Documentation only docs(sop): add Claude session context template

💡 AI-assisted commits: Add ai-assisted: yes to the commit footer so reviewers know to apply extra scrutiny to the diff.

docs.title: 7.1 PR Checklist — Author
docs.text:
• Branch is up to date with develop (rebase or merge before opening PR).
  • All tests pass locally.
  • No console.logs, TODO comments, or dead code left from Claude output.
  • PR description explains what changed and why, not just what Claude said.
  • If AI-assisted: note which files were substantially generated by Claude.
  • Self-review the diff in GitHub before requesting reviewers.

docs.title: 7.2 PR Checklist — Reviewer
docs.text:
• Verify the logic, not just the style — AI-generated code can be syntactically correct but semantically wrong.
  • Check that type signatures and interfaces are consistent with the shared codebase.
  • Confirm any SQL or pgvector queries run the EXPLAIN ANALYZE path before merging.
  • Leave inline comments for any concerns; do not merge with unresolved threads.

docs.title: 7.3 Merge Rules
docs.text: Item Details Minimum reviewers 1 for feature branches, 2 for changes to shared types or DB schema Merge strategy Squash merge into develop; rebase merge into main Branch deletion Delete branch after merge CI required All status checks must pass before merge is enabled

docs.title: 8.1 High-Risk Files — Extra Caution Required
docs.text:
⚠️ Warning: These files are conflict hotspots. Coordinate via your team channel before asking Claude to modify them.

  • Database migration files (supabase/migrations/*)
  • Shared type definitions and interfaces (types/*.ts)
  • Environment config and constants files
  • Package manifests (package.json, package-lock.json)
  • Shared utility modules used by multiple features

docs.title: 8.2 Coordination Rules
docs.text:
1. Announce in the team channel before starting a session that touches high-risk files.
  2. Never run two concurrent Claude sessions targeting the same file. Finish, commit, push — then let a teammate pull before they start.
  3. If a conflict occurs during rebase, resolve it manually. Do not ask Claude to auto-resolve merge conflicts without understanding the diff first.
  4. Keep migration files immutable after they land on develop. Create a new migration instead of editing an existing one.

docs.title: 8.3 Daily Sync Habit
docs.text:
Start every working day with:

git fetch origin && git rebase origin/develop

This keeps your branch current and surfaces conflicts early when they are easiest to fix.

docs.title: 9.1 Always Supply to Claude
docs.text:
• Existing type definitions for any entity Claude will touch.
  • Naming conventions (e.g. snake_case for DB, camelCase for TS, kebab-case for files).
  • The project's validation library (e.g. Zod schemas) so Claude generates compatible code.
  • Any shared utility functions Claude might otherwise re-implement.

docs.title: 9.2 Review Checklist for AI-Generated Code
docs.text: Area What to check Naming Matches project conventions (checked against existing files) Imports No unused imports; no imports of non-existent modules Error handling Follows the project's error handling pattern (not ad-hoc try/catch) Types No implicit any; types match shared interfaces Logging Uses project logger, not console.log Env vars Accessed via the project's config module, not process.env directly Tests At minimum a happy path and one error case

docs.title: 9.3 Linting & Formatting
docs.text:
Claude output should be run through the formatter before committing. Set up a pre-commit hook if not already in place:

# .husky/pre-commit
npx lint-staged  # runs eslint + prettier on staged files

docs.title: 10. Security & Secrets
docs.text:
🔒 Critical: Never paste real credentials, connection strings, or API keys into a Claude session. Use placeholder values and substitute locally.

  • Supabase URLs and keys: use SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY placeholders in prompts.
  • Do not share .env files in Claude — describe the shape of the config instead.
  • Review Claude output for any hardcoded strings that look like tokens or passwords before committing.
  • If you accidentally paste a secret into Claude.ai, rotate the credential immediately.

docs.title: 11. Quick Reference — Do's and Don'ts
docs.text:
✅ Do ❌ Don't Pull & rebase before every Claude session Start a session on a stale branch Use one branch per ticket / task Accumulate multiple unrelated changes in one branch Review every line of AI output before committing Bulk-commit Claude output without a diff review Supply context: schema, types, conventions Expect Claude to remember previous sessions Note "ai-assisted" in PR description and commit footer Hide AI involvement from reviewers Coordinate on shared files in team channel first Edit migration files or shared types without announcing Run tests and linter after every Claude session Commit code that hasn't been executed locally Use placeholder values for secrets in prompts Paste real credentials into Claude

Alpha Four · Engineering SOP · v1.0 · Review quarterly or after major tooling changes
